statement.en: Mahishi is a demoness in Hindu mythology whose story concerns Ayyappa and Sabarimala.

basis_claims.quote: When Mahishi attempted to storm heaven once more, Ayyappan, then a young prince, ascended to the celestial realms. He engaged the demoness in a fierce battle, eventually catching her by her horns and hurling her down to Earth. She landed on the banks of the Azhuthayar River near Sabarimala, where Ayyappan performed a divine dance on her body as she died.

statement.id: Ayyappan menangkap tanduknya dan menjatuhkannya ke bumi dalam pertarungan.
statement.en: Ayyappan seizes her horns and casts her to Earth during their battle.

basis_claims.quote: The birth mission of Ayyappa was to eliminate the threat caused by Mahishi, a demoness.

statement.id: Kerala Tourism menjelaskan bahwa misi kelahiran Ayyappa adalah menghapus ancaman Mahishi.
statement.en: Kerala Tourism explains Ayyappa's birth mission as eliminating the threat posed by Mahishi.

additional_sources.basis: JRAI ethnography note4 identifies local-informant Mahishi as she-buffalo, distinct from male Mahishasura; source search excerpt inspected.

basis_claims.quote: Sarama (Sanskrit: सरमा, Saramā) or Devashuni (Sanskrit: देव-शुनी, Devaśunī) is a female dog of the gods in Hindu mythology. She first appears in one of Hinduism's earliest texts, the Rig Veda, in which she helps the king of the gods Indra to recover divine cows stolen by the Panis asuras. This legend is alluded to in many later texts, and Sarama is often associated with Indra.

statement.id: Dalam Rigveda ia membantu Indra menemukan sapi ilahi yang dicuri para Pani.
statement.en: In the Rigveda she helps Indra recover divine cows stolen by the Panis.

basis_claims.quote: Early Rig Vedic works do not directly call Sarama a "dog," but her actions, behavior, and onomatopoeia in R.V. 10.108 provide a vivid description of a dog's behavior, and dogs in the Rig Veda are often given the name Sarameya—daughters of Sarama. In addition later Vedic mythologies and interpretations also directly call Sarama as a dog.

statement.id: Teks Rigveda awal tidak langsung menyebutnya anjing; tafsir Weda belakangan menyebutnya demikian.
statement.en: Early Rigvedic texts do not directly call her a dog; later Vedic interpretations do.

basis_claims.quote: the mother of all dogs, in particular of the two four-eyed brindle dogs of the god Yama,

statement.id: Ia disebut ibu dua anjing Yama bermata empat dan berbulu belang.
statement.en: She is called mother of Yama's two four eyed brindled dogs.

basis_claims.quote: Sarama's other name Deva-shuni means "divine bitch" or "bitch of the gods".

statement.id: Sebutan Devashuni berarti anjing betina ilahi atau anjing betina para dewa.
statement.en: The epithet Devashuni means divine bitch or bitch of the gods.

basis_claims.quote: The story revolves around John Lambton, an heir of the Lambton Estate, County Durham (in ceremonial Tyne and Wear), and his battle with a giant worm (dragon) that had been terrorising the local villages.

basis_claims.quote: Eventually, the worm grows extremely large and the well becomes poisonous. The villagers start to notice livestock going missing and discover that the fully-grown worm has emerged from the well and coiled itself around a local hill.

statement.id: Cacing tumbuh besar, sumur beracun, ternak hilang, cacing melilit bukit (Worm Hill, Fatfield).
statement.en: The worm grows huge, the well turns poisonous, livestock vanish, the worm coils round a hill (Worm Hill, Fatfield) seven times.

basis_claims.quote: She tells him to cover his armour in spearheads and fight the worm in the River Wear, where it now spends its days wrapped around a great rock. The witch also tells John that after killing the worm he must then kill the first living thing he sees, or else his family will be cursed for nine generations and will not die in their beds.

statement.en: The witch (near Durham): spearhead-studded armour, fight in the Wear; kill the first living thing or nine generations are cursed.

basis_claims.quote: Susna (Sanskrit: शुष्ण, romanized: Śuṣṇa) is an asura described in Hindu texts. Normally associated with drought, Susna is often described as possessing a snake-like form with horns. He is an enemy of the deity Indra.

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan Vritra, asura lain yang menghalangi sungai.
statement.en: He is associated with Vritra, another asura obstructing rivers.

basis_claims.quote: To defeat the asura, Indra destroys Susna's fortress, and, at the request of his follower Kutsa, sends rains to end the drought, defeating the asura.

statement.en: In the Rigveda account Indra destroys Susna's fortress and sends rain at Kutsa's request.

barghest.depicted_variant: Black dog death-omen form at Troller's Gill

basis_claims.quote: In Northern English folklore, the Barghest or Barguest is a mythical monstrous black dog with large teeth and claws; however, in other cases, the name can refer to a ghost or household elf, especially in Northumberland and Durham, such as the Cauld Lad of Hylton.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris Utara (Northern English folklore), Barghest (Barguest) anjing hitam mengerikan bergigi dan bercakar besar, atau hantu atau elf rumah di Northumberland dan Durham, seperti Cauld Lad of Hylton.
statement.en: In Northern English folklore the Barghest (Barguest) is a monstrous black dog with large teeth and claws, or a ghost or household elf in Northumberland and Durham, like the Cauld Lad of Hylton.

basis_claims.quote: In Yorkshire, England, one notable case is said to frequent a remote gorge named Troller's Gill in the Yorkshire Dales. A ballad entitled "The Legend of the Troller's Gill" can be found in William Hone's Everyday Book (1830).

statement.id: Di Yorkshire (England), Barghest menghantui ngarai Troller's Gill di Yorkshire Dales; balada The Legend of the Troller's Gill ada dalam Everyday Book karya William Hone (1830).
statement.en: In Yorkshire, England, a Barghest haunts the gorge of Troller's Gill in the Yorkshire Dales; the ballad The Legend of the Troller's Gill is in William Hone's Everyday Book (1830).

basis_claims.quote: The Barghest often allegedly serves as an omen of death. At the passing of a notable person the Barghest may appear, followed by all the other dogs of the local area in a kind of funeral procession, heralding the person's death with howling and barking.

statement.id: Barghest pertanda kematian; saat tokoh meninggal ia muncul diikuti anjing-anjing setempat dalam semacam iring-iringan jenazah.
statement.en: The Barghest is an omen of death; at a notable death it appears followed by the local dogs in a funeral procession.

basis_claims.quote: Besides taking the form of a large black dog with fiery eyes, it may also become invisible and walk about with the sound of rattling chains. It may also foretell the death of an individual by lying across the threshold of his or her house, and like the vampire the Barghest is unable to cross rivers.

statement.id: Selain anjing hitam bermata api, ia dapat tak terlihat dengan bunyi rantai, meramalkan kematian dengan berbaring di ambang pintu, dan seperti vampir tak dapat menyeberangi sungai.
statement.en: Besides a fiery-eyed black dog it can go invisible with rattling chains, foretell death lying across a threshold, and like the vampire cannot cross rivers.

basis_claims.quote: The water bull, also known as tarbh-uisge in Scottish Gaelic, is a mythological Scottish creature similar to the Manx tarroo ushtey and the Irish tarbh-uisce. Generally regarded as a nocturnal resident of moorland lochs, it is usually more amiable than its equine counterpart the water horse, but has similar amphibious and shapeshifting abilities.

statement.id: Water bull (tarbh-uisge, Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic) makhluk mitologi Skotlandia (Scottish), mirip tarroo ushtey Manx dan tarbh-uisce Irlandia (Irish); penghuni malam loch; lebih ramah dari kuda air (Water horse); amfibi dan berubah wujud; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The water bull (Scottish Gaelic tarbh-uisge) is a Scottish creature like the Manx tarroo ushtey and Irish tarbh-uisce; a nocturnal loch dweller, kinder than the water horse, amphibious and shapeshifting.

basis_claims.quote: Lexicographer Edward Dwelly translates tarbh-uisge from the Scottish Gaelic as "water bull, sea bull or cow" with the addition of "fabulous" within parentheses.

statement.id: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-uisge banteng air, banteng laut atau sapi (Scottish Gaelic).
statement.en: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-uisge, water bull, sea bull or cow.

basis_claims.quote: The water bull is able to shapeshift into human form, and live on land or in water. It can be a monstrous, malevolent black beast, especially when described as a tarbh-uisge, but not as nasty as the each-uisge or water horse. It can also be amiable and sometimes helpful.

statement.id: Berubah menjadi manusia; bisa binatang hitam jahat, tak sejahat each-uisge (Each-uisge); bisa ramah.
statement.en: Shapeshifts into human form; may be a malevolent black beast, less nasty than the each-uisge; can be friendly.

basis_claims.quote: Belief in the existence of water bulls persisted in Scotland until at least the last quarter of the 19th century.

statement.id: Kepercayaan bertahan di Skotlandia (Scotland) hingga akhir abad ke-19.
statement.en: Belief persisted in Scotland until at least the late 19th century.

statement.id: Tanduk karkadann dipercaya memiliki daya penyembuhan.
statement.en: The karkadann’s horn is believed to have healing powers.

visual_requirements: One natural horse four hooves mane and tail
Running on sea surface without sinking
Swift windlike otherworld steed
Noble enchanted divine majesty

basis_claims.quote: is a horse in the Irish Mythological Cycle which could traverse both land and sea, swifter than wind-speed. The horse was the property of the sea-god Manannan mac Lir, but provided to Lugh Lamh-fada (Irish: Luġ Lámhfhada ) to use at his disposal. In the story Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann ("The Fate of the Children of Tuireann"), Lugh refused to lend it to the sons of Tuireann

statement.id: Enbarr (Énbarr, Aonbharr; Irlandia/Irish Aonbharr Mhanannáin) kuda Siklus Mitologi Irlandia, melintasi darat dan laut; milik Manannan mac Lir (Manannán mac Lir), dipakai Lugh Lamh-fada; Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann; Sguaba Tuinne; di Irlandia.
statement.en: Enbarr (Énbarr, Aonbharr; Irish Aonbharr Mhanannáin) is a horse of the Irish Mythological Cycle crossing land and sea; owned by Manannan mac Lir, used by Lugh Lamh-fada; Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann; Sguaba Tuinne.

basis_claims.quote: As a common noun enbarr is defined as "froth" in the medieval Cormac's glossary. The modern Irish form Aonbharr is glossed as "One Mane" by O'Curry

statement.id: Cormac's glossary: buih (froth); O'Curry: Satu Surai (One Mane); James Mackillop: supremasi unik.
statement.en: Cormac's glossary: froth; O'Curry: One Mane; James Mackillop: unique supremacy.

basis_claims.quote: The horse was quicker than the "naked cold wind of spring", and could travel over land or sea with equal ease. It also had the property that whoever was mounted on its back could not be killed.

statement.id: Lebih cepat dari angin dingin musim semi; penunggangnya tak dapat dibunuh.
statement.en: Quicker than the cold wind of spring; its rider could not be killed.

basis_claims.quote: Enbarr Manannán, atau Enbarr dengan surai menjuntai, (juga ditulis Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Aonbárr, Énbarr, Enbhárr; Irlandia Klasik: Aonḃaɼɼ Mhanannáin) adalah nama dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia dari kuda Lugh Lamh-fada

statement.id: Enbarr Manannán (Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Énbarr) kuda Lugh Lamh-fada dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia (Irlandia Klasik).
statement.en: Enbarr Manannán (Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Énbarr) is Lugh Lamh-fada's horse in the Irish Mythological Cycle.

herne-the-hunter.depicted_variant: Shakespeare/Windsor forest antlered ghost walking around oak
visual_requirements: Humanlike ghost with great stag antlers
Shaking chain
Winter midnight Windsor oak
Frightening haunted hunter aura

basis_claims.quote: In English folklore, Herne the Hunter is a ghost associated with Windsor Forest and Great Park in the English county of Berkshire. He is said to have antlers growing from his head, ride a horse, torment cattle, and rattle chains.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Herne the Hunter adalah hantu Windsor Forest dan Great Park di Berkshire, bertanduk rusa, menunggang kuda, menyiksa ternak, dan menggemerincingkan rantai.
statement.en: In English folklore Herne the Hunter is a ghost of Windsor Forest and Great Park in Berkshire, antlered, horse-riding, tormenting cattle and rattling chains.

basis_claims.quote: Doth all the winter-time, at still midnight Walk round about an oak, with great ragg'd horns; And there he blasts the tree, and takes the cattle, And makes milch-kine yield blood, and shakes a chain In a most hideous and dreadful manner.

statement.id: Shakespeare: sepanjang musim dingin, tengah malam, Herne mengelilingi pohon ek dengan tanduk besar, merusak pohon, membuat sapi perah (milch-kine) mengeluarkan darah, dan menggemerincingkan rantai.
statement.en: Shakespeare: all winter at midnight Herne walks round an oak with great ragged horns, blasts the tree, makes milch-kine yield blood and shakes a chain.

basis_claims.quote: Officially published versions of the play refer only to the tale of Herne as the ghost of a former Windsor Forest keeper who haunts a particular oak tree at midnight in the winter time.

statement.id: Versi resmi lakon menyebut Herne arwah bekas penjaga Windsor Forest yang menghantui pohon ek pada tengah malam di musim dingin.
statement.en: Official versions call Herne the ghost of a former Windsor Forest keeper haunting an oak at midnight in winter.

glashtyn.depicted_variant: Manx handsome human male with horse ears
visual_requirements: Handsome dark-skinned curly-haired human youth
Shining eyes
One pair horse ears replacing human ears
Dangerous alluring water aura

basis_claims.quote: Some tales or lore recount that it has pursued after women, ending in the stock motif of escape by cutting loose the skirt-hem, although in one modern version her escape is achieved by a rooster's crowing; in that tale the glashtin pretends to be a handsome man but is betrayed by his horse-ears.

statement.id: Mengejar perempuan yang lolos dengan memotong rok; dalam versi modern kokok ayam; menyamar lelaki tampan, terbongkar oleh telinga kuda.
statement.en: It chases women who escape by cutting their hem; in a modern version a rooster's crow; disguised as a handsome man, betrayed by horse-ears.

basis_claims.quote: Sous sa forme humaine, il apparait comme un très beau jeune homme avec des yeux brillants, une peau sombre et des cheveux bouclés. Il ne peut être distingué des êtres humains que par ses oreilles, qui restent pointues comme celles d'un cheval.

statement.id: Wujud manusia: pemuda tampan, mata berkilau, kulit gelap, rambut ikal; telinga runcing seperti kuda (cheval).
statement.en: In human form a handsome youth with shining eyes, dark skin and curly hair; ears pointed like a horse's (cheval).

visual_requirements: Pure natural raven morphology
Black shaggy corvid feathers
Night setting
Malevolent supernatural intelligence

basis_claims.quote: A valravn is a supernatural raven in Danish renaissance folklore. It principally appears in the folk ballad "Valravnen" (Danish: The Valravn ) where it is depicted as a knight who was transformed into a raven, and whose curse can only be broken by consuming the blood of a boy.

statement.id: Valravn adalah gagak gaib dalam cerita rakyat Denmark masa Renaisans yang terutama muncul dalam balada rakyat "Valravnen" sebagai ksatria yang diubah menjadi gagak, yang kutukannya hanya dapat dipatahkan dengan meminum darah anak lelaki.
statement.en: A valravn is a supernatural raven of Danish Renaissance folklore, appearing mainly in the ballad 'Valravnen' as a knight transformed into a raven whose curse can only be broken by drinking a boy's blood.

basis_claims.quote: Selon le folklore danois de la fin des années 1800, lorsqu'un roi ou un chef de guerre est tué dans une bataille et n'est pas enterré immédiatement, les corbeaux viennent et le dévorent. Cet acte les transforme en valraven. Le valraven qui a mangé le cœur du roi acquiert toute la connaissance de l'homme et peut alors accomplir des actes d'une grande malveillance

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat Denmark akhir abad ke-19, bila raja atau panglima gugur dalam perang dan tidak segera dikuburkan, gagak-gagak memakannya dan berubah menjadi valraven; yang memakan jantung raja memperoleh seluruh pengetahuannya dan dapat berbuat sangat jahat.
statement.en: In late-1800s Danish folklore, when a king or war chief was killed in battle and not buried at once, ravens devoured him and became valraven; the one that ate the king's heart gained all his knowledge and could do great evil.

basis_claims.quote: The raven flies at night, during the day he mustn't: ... Out then walked the nobleman and offered him castles so lovely: and in addition half his land, if only he could keep his son.

statement.id: Balada itu dibuka dengan larik bahwa gagak terbang di malam hari dan tak boleh terbang di siang hari; kelak sang bangsawan menawarkan istana-istana dan separuh negerinya agar boleh mempertahankan putranya.
statement.en: The ballad opens with the raven flying at night and forbidden by day; later the nobleman offers it lovely castles and half his land if only he may keep his son.

al-folklore.depicted_variant: Armenian Al/Hal with clay nose and fiery eyes
visual_requirements: Armenian clay-nosed demon variant
two fiery eyes
malicious nocturnal childbirth-demon aura

basis_claims.quote: is a class of demon in the folklore of the Caucasus, Armenia, Iran and Central Asia.

statement.id: Al atau Hal adalah golongan iblis cerita rakyat Kaukasus, Armenia, Iran, dan Asia Tengah.
statement.en: Al, or Hal, is a class of demons in Caucasian, Armenian, Iranian, and Central Asian folklore.

basis_claims.quote: Als are demons of childbirth, interfering with human reproduction.

statement.id: Al adalah iblis persalinan yang mengganggu kelahiran manusia.
statement.en: Als are childbirth demons interfering with human reproduction.

basis_claims.quote: In Armenian tradition, the all steal the lung, liver and heart of women in childbirth

statement.id: Tradisi Armenia menyebut al mencuri paru, hati, dan jantung perempuan yang melahirkan.
statement.en: Armenian tradition describes als stealing the lungs, liver, and heart of women giving birth.

basis_claims.quote: They have clay noses and fiery eyes

statement.id: Al dalam uraian Armenia memiliki hidung tanah liat dan mata berapi.
statement.en: Als in the Armenian account have clay noses and fiery eyes.

basis_claims.quote: Al (Hal) – nocturnal predator demons who fed on newborns

statement.id: Sumber pendamping menyebut Al atau Hal sebagai pemangsa malam yang memakan bayi.
statement.en: The accompanying source describes Al, or Hal, as nocturnal predators feeding on newborns.

alp-folklore.depicted_variant: Small black male nightmare spirit with concealment cap
visual_requirements: Small dark male human-shaped being
Tarnkappe cap of concealment
Nighttime bed setting and scale
Sinister oppressive nightmare aura

basis_claims.quote: An Alp is typically male, while the mara and mart appear to be more feminine versions of the same creature. Its victims are often females, whom it attacks during the night, controlling their dreams and creating horrible nightmares (hence the German word Alptraum ["elf-dream"], meaning a nightmare).

statement.id: Alp biasanya jantan, sedangkan mara dan mart tampaknya versi lebih feminin; korbannya sering perempuan yang diserangnya pada malam hari dengan mengendalikan mimpi mereka, dari situ kata Jerman Alptraum ("mimpi elf"), yaitu mimpi buruk.
statement.en: The Alp is typically male, the mara and mart appearing more feminine versions; its victims are often women whom it attacks at night by controlling their dreams, hence the German Alptraum ('elf-dream'), a nightmare.

basis_claims.quote: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and becomes heavier until the crushing weight awakens the terrified and breathless dreamer. The victim awakes unable to move under the Alp's weight.

statement.id: Alpdruck terjadi saat Alp duduk mengangkangi dada orang tidur dan makin berat hingga korban terbangun ketakutan dan sesak napas, tak bisa bergerak di bawah bebannya.
statement.en: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and grows heavier until the terrified, breathless dreamer wakes, unable to move under its weight.

basis_claims.quote: The hat is known as a Tarnkappe (the literal translation being "camouflage cap" or "cap of concealment") which is simply a hat (or less commonly a veil) that gives the Alp magic powers and the ability to turn invisible while worn ... An Alp who has lost this hat will offer a great reward for its safe return.

statement.id: Topi Alp disebut Tarnkappe ("topi penyamaran"), yang memberinya kekuatan gaib dan kemampuan tak terlihat selama dipakai; Alp yang kehilangan topi ini akan menawarkan imbalan besar untuk pengembaliannya.
statement.en: Its hat is called the Tarnkappe ('cap of concealment'), giving the Alp magic powers and invisibility while worn; an Alp that loses it will offer a great reward for its return.

basis_claims.quote: Nachtalb ist eine späte Bezeichnung für ein Fantasie- und Sagenwesen, das ursprünglich „Mahr“ hieß und in der Nacht auf Menschen lastet (vgl. Albtraum) und ihnen Grauen einflößt.

statement.id: Nachtalb adalah sebutan belakangan untuk makhluk khayalan dan legenda yang semula bernama Mahr, yang menindih manusia pada malam hari dan membuat mereka ngeri.
statement.en: Nachtalb is a late name for a fantasy and legendary being originally called Mahr that weighs on people at night and fills them with dread.

basis_claims.quote: Es handelt sich gewöhnlich um ein kleines, schwarzes Wesen, das schlafende Menschen und Haustiere anfällt, selten auch Gegenstände. Es dringt durch Schlüssel- oder Astlöcher ein.

statement.id: Makhluk ini biasanya kecil dan hitam, menyerang manusia dan hewan peliharaan yang tidur, jarang juga benda, dan masuk lewat lubang kunci atau lubang dahan.
statement.en: It is usually a small black being that attacks sleeping people and domestic animals, rarely objects, and enters through keyholes or knot-holes.

hafgufa.depicted_variant: Whale-like nostril/lower-jaw sea monster of late Orvar-Odd saga
visual_requirements: One immense whale-like aquatic sea beast
Nostril head and lower jaw as rock-like masses
Vast open surface mouth trap-feeding
Dreadful primordial ocean predatory aura
hafgufa.aura: Dreadful primordial ocean immensity and predatory menace

basis_claims.quote: Hafgufa (Old Norse: haf "sea" + Old Norse: gufa "steam"; "sea-reek"; "sea-steamer") is a sea creature, purported to inhabit Iceland's waters (Greenland Sea) and southward toward Helluland. Although it was thought to be a sea monster, research suggests that the stories originated from a specialized feeding technique among whales known as trap-feeding.

statement.id: Hafgufa (Nordik Kuno haf, "laut", + gufa, "uap") adalah makhluk laut yang konon menghuni perairan Islandia (Laut Greenland) hingga ke selatan menuju Helluland; meski dianggap monster laut, penelitian menduga kisahnya berasal dari teknik makan paus yang disebut trap-feeding.
statement.en: Hafgufa (Old Norse haf 'sea' + gufa 'steam') is a sea creature said to inhabit Iceland's waters (the Greenland Sea) and south toward Helluland; though thought a sea monster, research suggests the stories came from a whale feeding technique called trap-feeding.

basis_claims.quote: In the Snorra Edda, the hafgufa ("sea-steamer") appears in the list (þulur) of whales. The spelling is also hafgúa in some copies.

statement.id: Dalam Snorra Edda, hafgufa muncul dalam daftar (þulur) paus; di beberapa salinan ejaannya hafgúa.
statement.en: In the Snorra Edda the hafgufa appears in the list (þulur) of whales; some copies spell it hafgúa.

basis_claims.quote: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga dating to the late 14th century, hafgufa is described as the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl ) of all, which fed on whales, ships, men, and anything it could catch ... it was the nostril and lower jaw which they had sailed in-between, although they mistook these for two massive rocks rising from the sea.

statement.id: Dalam versi akhir Örvar-Odds saga dari akhir abad ke-14, hafgufa adalah monster laut (sjóskrímsl) terbesar yang memangsa paus, kapal, manusia, dan apa saja; awak kapal berlayar di antara lubang hidung dan rahang bawahnya, yang mereka kira dua batu besar.
statement.en: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga from the late 14th century hafgufa is the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl), feeding on whales, ships, men and anything else; the crew sailed between its nostril and lower jaw, mistaking them for two great rocks.

basis_claims.quote: Once a large number had crowded into its mouth and belly, it would close its mouth and devour them all at once.

statement.id: Setelah banyak ikan berdesakan di mulut dan perutnya, ia menutup mulut dan melahap semuanya sekaligus.
statement.en: Once many fish had crowded into its mouth and belly, it shut its mouth and devoured them all at once.

visual_requirements: Dragon-dog quadruped
Dog paws and dragon scales neck tail
Hornless conservative selected morphology
Peaceful vigilant huabiao guardian

basis_claims.quote: is a Chinese legendary creature that is sometimes described as a half-dragon and half-dog.

statement.id: Denglong adalah makhluk legenda Tiongkok yang kadang digambarkan setengah naga dan setengah anjing.
statement.en: Denglong is a Chinese legendary creature sometimes depicted as half dragon and half dog.

basis_claims.quote: Some legends list Denglong as one of the sons of the Dragon King, and it is associated with guardianship.

statement.id: Beberapa legenda menyebutnya salah satu putra Raja Naga dan mengaitkannya dengan penjagaan.
statement.en: Some legends call it a Dragon King's son and associate it with guardianship.

basis_claims.quote: Denglongs are featured on top of Huabiaos, including one inside of and one outside of Tiananmen Gate. The Denglong inside the gate is named Wangdigui (expecting the emperor to come back soon) and faces North, indicating the emperor should not get distracted by the scenery outside the palace and should instead return to manage the state affairs.

statement.id: Patungnya terdapat di atas huabiao di dalam dan luar Gerbang Tiananmen.
statement.en: Its figures stand atop huabiao inside and outside Tiananmen Gate.

basis_claims.quote: a beast called “Wangtianhou”, which in Chinese mythology, is one of the Nine Sons of Dragon.

statement.id: Peking University menyebut Wangtianhou sebagai salah satu sembilan putra naga.
statement.en: Peking University identifies Wangtianhou as one of the dragon's nine sons.

cath-palug.depicted_variant: Welsh monstrous cat by Menai Strait
visual_requirements: Monstrous enormous feline
One cat head four paws and long tail
Near Welsh water
Fearsome plague-cat aura

basis_claims.quote: was a monstrous cat in Welsh mythology associated with Arthurian legend. Given birth to in Gwynedd by the pig Henwen of Cornwall, the cat was to haunt the Isle of Anglesey until Kay went to the island to hunt it down. Outside of Wales, the cat's opponent has been transposed to King Arthur himself or, occasionally, other legendary heroes such as Ogier the Dane.

statement.id: Cath Palug (Cath Paluc, Cath Balug, Cath Balwg; Kucing Palug) kucing raksasa mitologi Wales (Welsh), legenda Arthurian; lahir di Gwynedd dari Henwen dari Cornwall; menghantui Anglesey (Isle of Anglesey) sampai Kay memburunya; di luar Wales lawannya Raja Arthur (King Arthur) atau Ogier the Dane; Chapalu (French, Prancis); di Britania dan Prancis.
statement.en: Cath Palug (Palug's Cat) was a monstrous cat of Welsh myth, born in Gwynedd to Henwen of Cornwall, haunting Anglesey until Kay hunted it; elsewhere its foe is King Arthur or Ogier the Dane.

basis_claims.quote: Cath Palug is always localised near water, such as the lakes of Lac du Bourget and Lake Geneva in France (cf. also § Local lore), or the sea in Wales.

statement.id: Selalu dekat air: Lac du Bourget, Danau Jenewa (Lake Geneva), Prancis (France), atau laut di Wales.
statement.en: Always near water: Lac du Bourget, Lake Geneva in France, or the sea in Wales.

basis_claims.quote: According to this source, it started life as a kitten (lit "whelp" ), given birth by the great white sow Henwen at the black rock in Llanfair [cy]. There the kitten was cast into the sea, but it crossed the Menai Strait and was found on Ynys Môn (Anglesey), where the sons of Palug raised it, not realizing the cat was to become one of the three great plagues of the island.

statement.id: Welsh Triads: lahir dari Henwen di Llanfair, dibuang ke laut, menyeberangi Selat Menai (Menai Strait) ke Anglesey (Ynys Môn), dibesarkan putra Palug; tiga wabah pulau.
statement.en: Welsh Triads: born to Henwen at Llanfair, cast into the sea, crossed the Menai Strait to Anglesey (Ynys Môn), raised by Palug's sons; one of the island's three plagues.

basis_claims.quote: Le Chapalu, Capalu ou Capalus est un chat monstrueux dont parlent des manuscrits médiévaux français rattachés à la légende arthurienne.

statement.id: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) kucing raksasa (chat monstrueux) dalam naskah abad pertengahan Prancis (français) legenda Arthurian.
statement.en: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) is a monstrous cat (chat monstrueux) in medieval French (français) Arthurian manuscripts.

huma-bird.depicted_variant: Conservative airborne Huma with auspicious shadow; no prescribed species/color asserted
visual_requirements: conservative interpretive bird shape with ordinary coherent avian anatomy
airborne never landing
visible auspicious bird shadow and beneficent aura

basis_claims.quote: is a mythical bird of Iranian legends and fables

statement.id: Huma adalah burung mitos dalam legenda dan fabel Iran.
statement.en: The huma is a mythical bird of Iranian legends and fables.

basis_claims.quote: a common motif in Sufi and Diwan poetry.

statement.id: Huma menjadi motif yang sering muncul dalam puisi Sufi dan Diwan.
statement.en: The huma is a recurring motif in Sufi and Diwan poetry.

basis_claims.quote: the bird is said never to alight on the ground

statement.id: Huma dipercaya tidak pernah hinggap di tanah.
statement.en: The huma is believed never to alight on the ground.

basis_claims.quote: its shadow (or touch) is said to be auspicious.

statement.id: Bayangan atau sentuhan huma dianggap membawa keberuntungan.
statement.en: The huma’s shadow or touch is considered auspicious.

bahkauv.depicted_variant: Aachen hot-spring calf monster, bear paws and scaly tail
visual_requirements: Shaggy deformed calf with fangs
Bear-like clawed paws and long scaly tail
Aachen hot spring drain setting
Ominous nonlethal lurking

basis_claims.quote: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to reside in Aachen, Germany. The creature has been featured in the folklore of both Aachen and the Rhineland. Often depicted as a deformed calf with fangs, the Bahkauv is commonly associated with drunken men.

statement.id: Bahkauv adalah monster mitos yang konon tinggal di Aachen, Jerman, muncul dalam cerita rakyat Aachen dan Rheinland, sering digambarkan sebagai anak sapi cacat bertaring, dan dikaitkan dengan lelaki mabuk.
statement.en: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to live in Aachen, Germany, featured in Aachen and Rhineland folklore, often shown as a deformed fanged calf and associated with drunken men.

basis_claims.quote: The Bahkauv is typically described as being similar to an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs. According to legend, the creature often lurks near fountains, streams, and sewers. The Aachen city sewers and the many thermal springs found under the city have been cited as a dwelling place for the Bahkauv.

statement.id: Bahkauv biasanya digambarkan seperti anak sapi memanjang atau cacat bertaring tajam; menurut legenda ia sering mengintai di dekat mata air, sungai kecil, dan selokan, dan saluran pembuangan serta mata air panas di bawah Aachen disebut sebagai tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: The Bahkauv is typically described as an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs; legend says it lurks near fountains, streams and sewers, and Aachen's sewers and hot springs are cited as its home.

basis_claims.quote: Nach dieser Sage hauste das Bahkauv in dem Abwasserkanal der Thermalquellen am Büchel, dem so genannten Kolbert. Seine Gestalt glich einem großen Kalb mit einem zottigen Fell. Im Maul hatte es scharfe Zähne, und seine klobigen Augen leuchteten im Dunkeln. Seine Pfoten sahen aus wie Bärentatzen mit scharfen Krallen, und sein Schweif war geschuppt

statement.id: Menurut sage, Bahkauv tinggal di saluran buangan mata air panas di Büchel yang disebut Kolbert; wujudnya seperti anak sapi besar berbulu kusut, bergigi tajam, bermata menyala dalam gelap, bercakar seperti beruang, dan berekor bersisik.
statement.en: By the legend the Bahkauv lived in the drain of the hot springs at the Büchel, the Kolbert; it looked like a large shaggy calf with sharp teeth, eyes glowing in the dark, bear-like clawed paws and a scaly tail.

basis_claims.quote: Das Bahkauv hat aber nie jemanden umgebracht und auch Frauen und Kinder nie belästigt.

statement.id: Namun Bahkauv tak pernah membunuh siapa pun dan tak pernah mengganggu perempuan maupun anak-anak.
statement.en: But the Bahkauv never killed anyone and never troubled women or children.

germanic-dragon.depicted_variant: Ancient legless wingless serpentine Germanic wyrm
visual_requirements: One giant serpentine wyrm
No legs or wings
Fangs and scales
Treasure guarding cave

basis_claims.quote: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English: wyrm ; Old Norse: ormr ; Old High German: wurm ), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons (Old English: draca ; Old Norse: dreki/*draki ; Old High German: trahho ) in the wider Germanic mythology and folklore, in which they are often portrayed as large venomous snakes and hoarders of gold.

statement.id: Worm, wurm, atau wyrm (Inggris Kuno wyrm, Nordik Kuno ormr, Jerman Hulu Kuno wurm), berarti "ular", adalah istilah kuno untuk naga dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Jermanik, yang sering digambarkan sebagai ular besar berbisa dan penimbun emas.
statement.en: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English wyrm, Old Norse ormr, Old High German wurm), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons in Germanic mythology and folklore, often shown as large venomous snakes hoarding gold.

basis_claims.quote: In Germaanske draak is in mytysk bist ôfkomstich út 'e mytology en folkloare fan 'e Germaanske folken, dat kwa skaaimerken sterk ôfwykt fan hoe't in draak ornaris foarsteld wurdt. Ynstee fan in mei skobben bepânsere lichem mei fjouwer poaten, in lange sturt en twa flearmûseftige wjukken op 'e rêch hat in Germaanske draak de foarm fan in gigantyske slange, sûnder poaten of wjukken.

statement.id: Naga Jermanik adalah hewan mitos dari mitologi dan cerita rakyat bangsa Jermanik yang cirinya sangat berbeda dari gambaran naga biasa: bukannya bertubuh bersisik berkaki empat, berekor panjang, dan bersayap kelelawar, ia berbentuk ular raksasa tanpa kaki atau sayap.
statement.en: The Germanic dragon (Germaanske draak) is a mythical beast of Germanic peoples' mythology and folklore that differs sharply from the usual dragon: instead of a scaly four-legged body, long tail and bat wings, it has the form of a gigantic snake (gigantyske slange) without legs (poaten) or wings (wjukken).

basis_claims.quote: The association between dragons and hoards of treasure is widespread in Germanic literature ... In the Völsung Cycle, Fáfnir , upon claiming a hoard of treasure, including the ring Andvaranaut, transforms into a dragon to protect and brood over it.

statement.id: Kaitan naga dengan timbunan harta tersebar luas dalam sastra Jermanik; dalam siklus Völsung, Fáfnir yang menguasai timbunan harta, termasuk cincin Andvaranaut, berubah menjadi naga untuk menjaga dan mengeraminya.
statement.en: The link between dragons and treasure hoards is widespread in Germanic literature; in the Völsung Cycle Fáfnir, having claimed a hoard including the ring Andvaranaut, becomes a dragon to guard and brood over it.

salmon-of-knowledge.depicted_variant: Living Irish salmon of wisdom before capture
visual_requirements: One natural salmon
Hazelnut tree and wisdom water context
Silver fish anatomy
Ancient profound knowledge aura

basis_claims.quote: The Salmon of Knowledge (Irish: An Bradán Feasa ) is a creature in the Fenian Cycle of Irish mythology, sometimes identified with the mythical seer Fintan mac Bóchra who was known as "The Wise" and was once transformed into a salmon.

statement.id: Salmon of Knowledge (Irlandia, Irish: An Bradán Feasa), makhluk Siklus Fenian (Fenian Cycle), kadang disamakan dengan Fintan mac Bóchra Sang Bijak (The Wise); di Irlandia.
statement.en: The Salmon of Knowledge (Irish An Bradán Feasa) is a creature of the Fenian Cycle, sometimes identified with Fintan mac Bóchra the Wise.

basis_claims.quote: In the story, an ordinary salmon ate nine hazelnuts that fell into the Well of Wisdom (an Tobar Segais) from nine hazel trees that surrounded the well. By this act, the salmon gained all the world's knowledge. The first person to eat of its flesh would in turn gain this knowledge.

statement.id: Dalam The Boyhood Deeds of Fionn, salmon biasa memakan sembilan buah hazel yang jatuh ke Well of Wisdom dan memperoleh seluruh pengetahuan dunia.
statement.en: In The Boyhood Deeds of Fionn, a salmon ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Well of Wisdom and gained all the world's knowledge.

basis_claims.quote: Fionn ate the salmon and in so doing gained all the knowledge of the world. For the rest of his life, Fionn could draw upon this knowledge merely by biting his thumb. The deep knowledge and wisdom gained from the Salmon of Knowledge allowed Fionn to become the leader of the Fianna

statement.id: Fionn memperoleh seluruh pengetahuan, memanggilnya dengan menggigit ibu jari, dan menjadi pemimpin Fianna.
statement.en: Fionn gained all knowledge, drew on it by biting his thumb, and became leader of the Fianna.

basis_claims.quote: est à l'origine un saumon ordinaire, qui mange les neuf noisettes tombés de l'arbre du savoir dans le fleuve Boyne — ou parfois le Shannon. Ce faisant, le saumon devient énorme et acquiert tout le savoir du monde, devenant plus sage que les hommes.

statement.id: Saumon de la sagesse memakan sembilan buah hazel yang jatuh ke Sungai Boyne atau Shannon, menjadi sangat besar dan tahu segalanya.
statement.en: The Saumon de la sagesse ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Boyne or Shannon, grew enormous and knew everything.

visual_requirements: Monstrous short thickset goblin
Long teeth and eagle-like hand talons
Red eyes and cap, iron boots
Left-hand pikestaff

basis_claims.quote: The redcap (or powrie) is a type of malevolent, murderous goblin found in folklore of the Anglo-Scottish border region. The redcap is said to inhabit ruined castles along the Anglo-Scottish border, especially those that were the scenes of tyranny or wicked deeds, and is known for soaking his cap in the blood of his victims. He is also known as Redcomb and Bloody Cap.

statement.id: Redcap (powrie) goblin pembunuh perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish), menghuni kastel runtuh, merendam topi dalam darah; juga Redcomb, Bloody Cap; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The redcap (powrie) is a murderous goblin of the Anglo-Scottish border, haunting ruined castles and soaking its cap in blood; also Redcomb, Bloody Cap.

basis_claims.quote: Redcap is depicted as "a short, thickset old elf with long prominent teeth, skinny fingers armed with talons like eagles, large eyes of a fiery red colour, grisly hair streaming down his shoulders, iron boots, a pikestaff in his left hand, and a red cap on his head".

statement.id: Elf tua pendek, gigi panjang, cakar elang, mata merah, sepatu besi, tongkat tombak, topi merah.
statement.en: A short old elf with long teeth, eagle talons, red eyes, iron boots, pikestaff and red cap.

visual_requirements: Woman upper body
Young salmon grilse tail instead of legs
Two arms no human legs
Scottish water spirit

basis_claims.quote: The ceasg [kʲʰɛsk] is a mermaid in Scottish folklore with the upper body of a beautiful woman merging with the tail of a grilse (a young salmon). She is also known in Scottish Gaelic as maighdean na tuinne ("maid of the wave") or maighdean mhara ("maid of the sea").

statement.id: Ceasg putri duyung folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Skotlandia), tubuh perempuan cantik berekor grilse; disebut maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara dalam Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic).
statement.en: The ceasg is a mermaid of Scottish folklore with a woman's body and a grilse tail; called maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara in Scottish Gaelic.

visual_requirements: Hideous true revenant form
Both feet point backward
South Asian tree/woodland setting
Vengeful predatory aura

basis_claims.quote: is a mythical or legendary creature resembling a woman, which may be a demonical revenant said to occur in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Caribbean, particularly popular in India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, and Suriname.

statement.id: Churel adalah makhluk mitis berwujud perempuan, mungkin mayat hidup yang jahat, yang dikenal di Asia Selatan, Asia Tenggara, dan Karibia, terutama di India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad dan Tobago, Guyana, dan Suriname.
statement.en: The churel is a mythical woman-like creature, perhaps a demonic revenant, found in South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Caribbean, especially India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana and Suriname.

basis_claims.quote: The churel is typically described as  "the ghost of an unpurified living thing", but because she is often said to latch on to trees, she is also called a tree-spirit. According to some legends, a woman who dies very cruelly will come back as a revenant churel for revenge, particularly targeting the males in her family.

statement.id: Churel biasa disebut "hantu makhluk hidup yang tidak disucikan", juga roh pohon karena sering menempel di pohon; menurut sebagian legenda perempuan yang mati secara kejam kembali sebagai churel untuk membalas dendam, terutama kepada lelaki dalam keluarganya.
statement.en: The churel is usually called 'the ghost of an unpurified living thing', also a tree-spirit since she clings to trees; by some legends a woman who dies cruelly returns as a churel for revenge, especially on the men of her family.

basis_claims.quote: The churel is mostly described as extremely ugly and hideous but is able to shape-shift and disguise herself as a beautiful woman to lure men into the woods or mountains where she either kills them or sucks up their life-force or virility, turning them into old men. Their feet are believed to be turned the other way around, so the toes face the direction of their back.

statement.id: Churel biasanya sangat buruk rupa, tetapi dapat menyamar sebagai perempuan cantik untuk memikat lelaki ke hutan atau gunung, lalu membunuh mereka atau mengisap daya hidupnya hingga menjadi tua; kakinya menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: The churel is usually hideous but can disguise herself as a beautiful woman to lure men into the woods or hills, where she kills them or drains their life force until they turn old; her feet point backwards.

visual_requirements: Three arms without hands or fingers
Three yellow red blue eyes
One stubby horn, gray hair and beard
Five rows teeth and two legs

basis_claims.quote: The cuegle is a monster in Cantabrian folklore. Walking on two legs and roughly humanoid in shape, it is believed to have black skin, a long beard, grey hair, three arms without hands or fingers, five rows of teeth, a single stubby horn and three eyes in its head: one yellow, one red, and one blue.

statement.id: Cuegle adalah monster cerita rakyat Cantabria yang berjalan dengan dua kaki dan berwujud mirip manusia, berkulit hitam, berjanggut panjang, berambut kelabu, bertangan tiga tanpa telapak atau jari, bergigi lima baris, bertanduk satu yang pendek, dan bermata tiga: kuning, merah, dan biru.
statement.en: The cuegle is a monster of Cantabrian folklore, two-legged and roughly humanlike, with black skin, a long beard, grey hair, three arms without hands or fingers, five rows of teeth, one stubby horn and three eyes: yellow, red and blue.

basis_claims.quote: El Cuegle puede ver cada uno, pasado, presente y futuro. El futuro lo ve con el ojo de la frente, el presente con el derecho y el pasado con el izquierdo.

statement.id: Cuegle dapat melihat masa lalu, kini, dan depan: masa depan dengan mata di dahi, masa kini dengan mata kanan, dan masa lalu dengan mata kiri.
statement.en: The cuegle can see past, present and future: the future with its forehead eye, the present with its right eye and the past with its left.

visual_requirements: Brown plesiosaur-like loch monster
Three visible humps
Loch Morar setting
Daunting elusive aquatic aura
morag-lake-monster.aura: Elusive and imposing dark-water lake monster

basis_claims.quote: is the nickname given to a loch monster believed by many to live in Loch Morar, Scotland. After Nessie, it is among the most written about of Scotland's legendary monsters. "Morag", a Scottish female name, is a pun on the name of the loch.

statement.id: Morag (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic Mòrag) monster Loch Morar, Skotlandia (Scotland); setelah Nessie paling banyak ditulis; nama perempuan Skotlandia (Scottish) sebagai permainan kata; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: Morag (Scottish Gaelic Mòrag) is a monster of Loch Morar, Scotland; after Nessie the most written about; a Scottish name punning on the loch.

basis_claims.quote: A widely reported claim from August 1969 involved two local men, Duncan McDonell and William Simpson, and their boat, with which they claimed to have accidentally struck the creature, prompting it to attack them. McDonell defended with an oar, and Simpson opened fire with his rifle, whereupon it sank slowly out of sight.

statement.id: Agustus 1969: Duncan McDonell dan William Simpson menabraknya, McDonell dengan dayung, Simpson menembak; cokelat, 7,6–9,1 m, tiga punuk.
statement.en: August 1969: Duncan McDonell and William Simpson struck it; McDonell used an oar, Simpson fired a rifle; brown, 7.6–9.1 m, three humps.

basis_claims.quote: Mhorag [ ˈvɔrak] (gälisch: Geist des Sees), auch Morag oder Maggie, ist der Name eines plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers, das angeblich im Loch Morar in Schottland leben soll.

statement.id: Mhorag (roh danau, gälisch), juga Morag atau Maggie, monster danau mirip plesiosaurus (plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers) di Loch Morar, Skotlandia (Schottland).
statement.en: Mhorag (Gaelic spirit of the loch), also Morag or Maggie, is a plesiosaur-like lake monster (plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers) in Loch Morar, Scotland (Schottland).

basis_claims.quote: Die Mhorag wird als sechs bis neun Meter langes Monster mit Höckern beschrieben und weist dadurch große Ähnlichkeit mit dem Ungeheuer von Loch Ness auf.

statement.id: Panjang 6–9 m berpunuk (Höckern), mirip monster Loch Ness (Ungeheuer von Loch Ness, Loch Ness Monster).
statement.en: 6–9 m long with humps (Höckern), very like the Loch Ness Monster (Ungeheuer von Loch Ness).

hamingja.depicted_variant: Animal guardian form, inspired by Bodvar Bjarki spirit-bear example
visual_requirements: Norse guardian in fully animal spirit-bear form
Natural bear anatomy
Protective powerful ancestral aura

basis_claims.quote: The hamingja was a type of female guardian spirit in Norse mythology. It was believed that she accompanied a person and decided their luck and happiness. Consequently, the name was also used to indicate happiness, and that is what it means in modern Icelandic. When a person died, the hamingja passed to a beloved family member

statement.id: Hamingja adalah jenis roh pelindung perempuan dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini menyertai seseorang dan menentukan untung serta kebahagiaannya; karena itu namanya juga berarti kebahagiaan, seperti dalam bahasa Islandia modern, dan saat orang itu meninggal, hamingja beralih kepada anggota keluarga tercinta.
statement.en: The hamingja was a type of female guardian spirit in Norse mythology believed to accompany a person and decide their luck and happiness; hence the word also means happiness, as in modern Icelandic, and when the person died it passed to a beloved family member.

basis_claims.quote: It was even possible to lend one's own hamingja to a friend, as happened when Hjalti Skeggiason was about to leave on a perilous voyage and asked Olaf II of Norway to lend him his hamingja. It usually appears during sleep in the form of an animal. It can also be the spirit of a sleeping person who appears in the form of an animal, as Bödvar Bjarki in the saga of Hrólfr Kraki.

statement.id: Hamingja bisa dipinjamkan kepada teman, seperti saat Hjalti Skeggiason hendak berlayar berbahaya dan meminta Olaf II dari Norwegia meminjamkan hamingja-nya; ia biasanya muncul saat tidur berwujud hewan, atau bisa berupa roh orang tidur dalam rupa hewan, seperti Bödvar Bjarki dalam saga Hrólfr Kraki.
statement.en: One's hamingja could be lent to a friend, as when Hjalti Skeggiason, before a perilous voyage, asked Olaf II of Norway to lend him his; it usually appears in sleep as an animal, or can be a sleeping person's spirit in animal form, like Bödvar Bjarki in the saga of Hrólfr Kraki.

basis_claims.quote: In Norse mythology, hamingja (Old Norse "luck") refers to two concepts: the personification of the good fortune or luck of an individual or family, the altered appearance of shape-shifters. Both Andy Orchard and Rudolf Simek note parallels between the concept of the hamingja and the fylgja.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, hamingja (Nordik Kuno, "keberuntungan") merujuk pada dua konsep: perwujudan untung baik seseorang atau keluarga, dan rupa yang berubah dari pengubah wujud; Andy Orchard dan Rudolf Simek mencatat kemiripannya dengan fylgja.
statement.en: In Norse mythology hamingja (Old Norse 'luck') refers to two concepts: the personified good fortune of an individual or family, and the altered appearance of shape-shifters; Andy Orchard and Rudolf Simek note parallels with the fylgja.

visual_requirements: Cat-shaped Scandinavian milk thief
Hair and wood-shaving construction
Near wooden milk pail
Uncanny furtive familiar aura

basis_claims.quote: A troll cat is the familiar of a witch in Scandinavian folklore. Troll cats sucked milk from cows and spat it out in the witches' milk pails, and went into homes to lick up cream. Aside from cats, similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare, and ball-shaped troll ball.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, kucing troll adalah makhluk peliharaan penyihir yang mengisap susu sapi dan memuntahkannya ke ember susu penyihir serta masuk ke rumah untuk menjilat krim; makhluk serupa antara lain kelinci susu, terwelu susu, dan bola troll.
statement.en: In Scandinavian folklore the troll cat is a witch's familiar that sucked cows' milk and spat it into the witch's pails and entered homes to lick cream; similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare and troll ball.

basis_claims.quote: Witches reportedly were able to create them from "human hair, nails, wood shavings, and the like" ... The Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa indicate their shapes: those troll cats looked like balls of yarn. Another kind of troll cat had the appearance of an ordinary cat; but, unlike the ball-shaped troll cat, harming the cat-shaped troll cat would result in the same harm to the witch.

statement.id: Penyihir konon membuatnya dari "rambut manusia, kuku, serutan kayu, dan semacamnya"; nama Norwegia trollnøste dan trollnøa menunjukkan wujud gulungan benang, sedangkan jenis lain tampak seperti kucing biasa, dan melukainya akan melukai penyihir juga.
statement.en: Witches reportedly made them from 'human hair, nails, wood shavings and the like'; the Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa show a ball-of-yarn shape, while another kind looked like an ordinary cat, and harming it harmed the witch too.

basis_claims.quote: Una bjära (mjölkhare, trollhare, pukhare, puken, trollkatten, baran, bärarn) era, en las creencias populares suecas, un ser característico que una bruja usaba para robar leche de las vacas de los vecinos. Una bjära podía ser una liebre (Småland), un gato o un pájaro (Dalarna) o un ovillo (Norrland).

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, bjära (juga mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten, dan lain-lain) adalah makhluk yang dipakai penyihir untuk mencuri susu sapi tetangga; ia bisa berwujud terwelu (Småland), kucing atau burung (Dalarna), atau gulungan benang (Norrland).
statement.en: In Swedish folk belief a bjära (also mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten and others) was a being a witch used to steal neighbours' cows' milk; it could be a hare (Småland), a cat or bird (Dalarna) or a ball of yarn (Norrland).

baldanders.depicted_variant: Sow form from Simplicius Simplicissimus transformation sequence
visual_requirements: Germanic protean creature in documented sow form
Full pig anatomy
Forest and cycle-of-transformation context
baldanders.aura: Uncanny protean intelligence in natural animal form

basis_claims.quote: Baldanders or Soon-Different is a creature of Germanic literary myth that features protean properties.

statement.id: Baldanders atau "Segera-Lain" adalah makhluk mitos sastra Jermanik yang bersifat protean.
statement.en: Baldanders or Soon-Different is a creature of Germanic literary myth with protean properties.

basis_claims.quote: is a character in the novel Simplicius Simplicissimus by Grimmelshausen, appearing in its Continuatio (1669) or Sixth Book. The character was appropriated from Hans Sachs's poem Baldanderst [sic] dated to 31 July 1534. Hans Sachs probably derived his "Baldanderst" from Proteus, the shapeshifter of classical Greco-Roman mythology.

statement.id: Baldanders adalah tokoh novel Simplicius Simplicissimus karya Grimmelshausen dalam Continuatio (1669) atau Buku Keenam, diambil dari puisi Hans Sachs Baldanderst bertanggal 31 Juli 1534; Sachs kemungkinan menurunkannya dari Proteus, pengubah wujud mitologi Yunani-Romawi.
statement.en: Baldanders is a character in Grimmelshausen's Simplicius Simplicissimus, in its Continuatio (1669) or Sixth Book, taken from Hans Sachs's poem Baldanderst dated 31 July 1534; Sachs probably derived it from Proteus, the Greco-Roman shapeshifter.

basis_claims.quote: Baldanders subsequently changes into a succession of forms: an oak tree, a sow, a bratwurst sausage, then a peasant's excrement, a meadow of clovers, cow dung (Kuhfladen ), a flower, mulberry tree, and silk carpet. ... in a natural cycle of things that perish and are reborn.

statement.id: Baldanders lalu berubah menjadi serangkaian wujud: pohon ek, babi betina, sosis bratwurst, kotoran, padang semanggi, kotoran sapi, bunga, pohon murbei, dan permadani sutra; urutan ini menggambarkan siklus alam tentang hal-hal yang binasa dan lahir kembali.
statement.en: Baldanders then changes into a series of forms: an oak, a sow, a bratwurst, excrement, a clover meadow, cow dung, a flower, a mulberry tree and a silk carpet; the sequence shows a natural cycle of things perishing and being reborn.

basis_claims.quote: According to Sachs’ and collected descriptions, the Baldanders is a creature that is symbolic for the continual change in nature and society

statement.id: Menurut uraian Sachs dan uraian lain yang dihimpun, Baldanders melambangkan perubahan terus-menerus dalam alam dan masyarakat.
statement.en: According to Sachs and collected descriptions, Baldanders symbolises continual change in nature and society.

skogsra.depicted_variant: Rear three quarter bark-bodied forest spirit with hollow wooden back, animal tail and one horse hoof
visual_requirements: Rear three quarter bark-bodied forest spirit with hollow wooden back, animal tail and one horse hoof

basis_claims.quote: appears in the form of a beautiful woman with a seemingly friendly temperament. She appears like a woman from the front but seen from behind she often has a tail and a hollow, rotten back, a human foot and a horse foot, and skin like tree bark.

statement.id: Ia tampil sebagai perempuan cantik yang tampak ramah; dari depan seperti perempuan, tetapi dari belakang sering berekor, berpunggung berongga dan busuk, berkaki satu manusia dan satu kuda, serta berkulit seperti kulit kayu.
statement.en: She appears as a beautiful, seemingly friendly woman; from the front like a woman, but from behind often with a tail, a hollow rotten back, one human foot and one horse foot, and skin like bark.

lutzelfrau.depicted_variant: Sheet-covered goat with horns, documented Bohemia/Tyrol Lucia manifestation
visual_requirements: Sheet-covered goat with horns, documented Bohemia/Tyrol Lucia manifestation

basis_claims.quote: According to a mid-19th century source, the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat, draped in a bedsheet with horns protruding out of the sheet. This is paralleled in Scandinavia.

statement.id: Menurut sumber pertengahan abad ke-19, Lusia di Bohemia dan Tirol tampil sebagai kambing yang berselubung seprai dengan tanduk mencuat, dan hal serupa ada di Skandinavia.
statement.en: According to a mid-19th-century source the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat draped in a bedsheet with horns poking out, paralleled in Scandinavia.

visual_requirements: Large black raven-like nocturnal creature
Raven head, beak, claws and two feathered wings
Dangerous night woodland aura

basis_claims.quote: Danish and Norwegian: nattravn ; Swedish: nattramn , nattkorp ; German: Nachtkrapp , Nachtrabe ) are creatures of European folklore, predominantly described as raven like creatures appearing in the night. The folklore differs regionally, and night ravens may be other beings, such as undead, shapeshifted into ravens.

statement.id: Gagak malam (Denmark/Norwegia: nattravn; Swedia: nattramn, nattkorp; Jerman: Nachtkrapp, Nachtrabe) adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Eropa yang umumnya digambarkan mirip gagak dan muncul di malam hari; ceritanya berbeda menurut daerah, gagak malam bisa juga makhluk lain seperti mayat hidup yang berubah menjadi gagak, dan kadang dipakai sebagai momok dalam kisah peringatan.
statement.en: Night ravens (Danish/Norwegian nattravn; Swedish nattramn, nattkorp; German Nachtkrapp, Nachtrabe) are creatures of European folklore, mostly raven-like beings appearing at night; the lore differs regionally, they may be other beings such as undead shapeshifted into ravens, and they are sometimes bugbears in cautionary tales.

basis_claims.quote: In German folklore (German: Nachtkrapp , Nachtrabe ), mainly of Southern Germany and Austria, the most common legends claim that the night raven leaves its hiding place at night to hunt. If it is seen by little children, it will abduct them into its nest and messily devour them ... According to other legends, the night raven will merely put children in his bag and take them away.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, terutama Jerman selatan dan Austria, gagak malam keluar dari persembunyiannya di malam hari untuk berburu; bila dilihat anak kecil, ia menculik mereka ke sarangnya dan memangsanya, sedangkan legenda lain menyebut ia hanya memasukkan anak ke karungnya dan membawanya pergi.
statement.en: In German folklore, mainly southern Germany and Austria, the night raven leaves its hiding place at night to hunt; if seen by small children it carries them to its nest and devours them, while other legends say it merely bags them and takes them away.

basis_claims.quote: Nachtkrabb oder Nacht(t)rapp ist im süddeutschen und österreichischen Raum der Name einer Kinderschreckfigur, die eine ähnliche Funktion wie der Sandmann erfüllt. Der Nachtkrabb greift sich angeblich Kinder, die sich nach Einbruch der Dunkelheit noch im Freien aufhalten ... Das fränkische Pendant nennt sich Nachtgiger.

statement.id: Nachtkrabb atau Nacht(t)rapp di Jerman selatan dan Austria adalah nama momok penakut anak dengan fungsi serupa Sandmann; ia konon menyambar anak yang masih di luar setelah gelap, dan padanannya di Franken disebut Nachtgiger.
statement.en: Nachtkrabb or Nacht(t)rapp is, in southern Germany and Austria, the name of a child-frightening figure with a function like the Sandman's; it supposedly snatches children still outdoors after dark, and its Franconian counterpart is the Nachtgiger.

basis_claims.quote: Krabb (auch Krapp, Krabbe, Grabbe, Rappe, von ahd. [h]raban) ist in oberdeutschen Dialekten eine Bezeichnung für den Raben oder andere Rabenvögel. Es lag nahe, dass diesen aasfressenden Schwarmvögeln auch allerhand unheilbringende Wirkung angedichtet wurde, zum Beispiel, dass der Rabe nachts die Kinder entführe.

statement.id: Krabb (juga Krapp, Krabbe, Rappe; dari Jerman Hulu Kuno [h]raban) dalam dialek Jerman Hulu berarti gagak atau burung sejenis; burung pemakan bangkai ini mudah dikaitkan dengan berbagai pengaruh buruk, misalnya menculik anak di malam hari.
statement.en: Krabb (also Krapp, Krabbe, Rappe; from Old High German [h]raban) in Upper German dialects means raven or other corvids; these carrion birds were readily credited with baleful deeds, such as the raven stealing children at night.

the-dragon-beowulf.depicted_variant: Winged fire-breathing treasure-keeper of Old English Beowulf
visual_requirements: One flying-and-crawling reptilian dragon
Fire breath and venomous teeth
Burial mound treasure
Vengeful avaricious aura
the-dragon-beowulf.aura: Evil destructive treasure guardian and avenging gold king

basis_claims.quote: rules wisely for fifty years until a slave awakens and angers a dragon by stealing a jeweled cup from its lair. When the angry dragon mercilessly burns the Geats' homes (including Beowulf's) and lands, Beowulf decides to fight and kill the monster personally. ... When the dragon wounds Beowulf fatally, Wiglaf attacks it with his sword, and Beowulf kills it with his dagger.

statement.id: Beowulf memerintah dengan bijak selama lima puluh tahun sampai seorang budak membangunkan dan membuat murka seekor naga dengan mencuri piala berpermata dari sarangnya; naga itu membakar rumah dan tanah kaum Geat, Beowulf memutuskan melawannya sendiri, dan ketika naga melukainya secara fatal, Wiglaf menyerang dengan pedang dan Beowulf membunuhnya dengan belati.
statement.en: Beowulf rules wisely for fifty years until a slave wakes and angers a dragon by stealing a jewelled cup from its lair; the dragon burns the Geats' homes and lands, Beowulf resolves to fight it himself, and when it wounds him fatally, Wiglaf strikes with his sword and Beowulf kills it with his dagger.

basis_claims.quote: Beowulf is the first piece of English literature to present a dragonslayer. Although the Beowulf dragon exhibits many existing motifs common to Germanic tradition, the Beowulf poet was the first to combine features and present a distinctive fire-breathing dragon. The Beowulf dragon was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937)

statement.id: Beowulf adalah karya sastra Inggris pertama yang menampilkan pembunuh naga; walau naganya memuat banyak motif umum tradisi Jermanik, penyair Beowulf yang pertama memadukannya menjadi naga penyembur api yang khas, dan naga ini diadaptasi untuk Dunia Tengah dalam The Hobbit (1937) karya J. R. R. Tolkien.
statement.en: Beowulf is the first English work to present a dragonslayer; though its dragon shows many common Germanic motifs, the poet was the first to combine them into a distinctive fire-breathing dragon, which was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937).

basis_claims.quote: Un dragon (draca ou wyrm en vieil anglais) est le troisième et dernier adversaire du héros Beowulf dans le poème épique anglo-saxon Beowulf. C'est l'un des premiers exemples connus de dragon européen dans la littérature. Il en possède toutes les caractéristiques : c'est un reptile maléfique, capable de voler et de ramper, qui crache du feu et dont la morsure est empoisonnée.

statement.id: Naga (draca atau wyrm dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno) adalah lawan ketiga dan terakhir Beowulf dalam epos Anglo-Saxon itu, salah satu contoh awal naga Eropa dalam sastra: reptil jahat yang bisa terbang dan merayap, menyembur api, dan gigitannya berbisa.
statement.en: The dragon (Old English draca or wyrm) is the third and last foe of Beowulf in the Anglo-Saxon epic, one of the earliest European literary dragons: an evil reptile able to fly and crawl, breathing fire, with a poisonous bite.

basis_claims.quote: Ce vol enrage le dragon qui dormait sur le trésor depuis trois cents ans, et il quitte son repaire pour semer la destruction dans le royaume des Geats en représailles.

statement.id: Pencurian itu membuat murka naga yang telah tidur di atas harta itu selama tiga ratus tahun, dan ia keluar dari sarangnya untuk menebar kehancuran di kerajaan Geat sebagai balasan.
statement.en: The theft enraged the dragon, which had slept on the treasure for three hundred years, and it left its lair to wreak destruction on the Geats' kingdom in revenge.

drude.depicted_variant: Drude soul in documented cat manifestation
visual_requirements: Drude soul in documented cat manifestation

basis_claims.quote: Hier sind Frauen, die dazu verdammt sind, sich jede Nacht ein Opfer zum Drücken suchen zu müssen: Erwachsene, Kinder und Haustiere werden heimgesucht, aber auch Bäume und Steine. ... kann als Geist durch kleinste Spalten und Schlüssellöcher in ein Zimmer dringen und dann in verschiedener Gestalt erscheinen (z. B. als Katze, Strohhalm oder Feder).

statement.id: Di Jerman selatan dan Austria, drude adalah perempuan yang dikutuk mencari korban setiap malam, orang dewasa, anak, hewan, juga pohon dan batu; rohnya masuk lewat celah dan lubang kunci dan tampil dalam berbagai rupa seperti kucing, sedotan, atau bulu.
statement.en: As drudes these pressing spirits are widespread in southern Germany and Austria: women condemned to find a victim each night, adults, children, animals, even trees and stones; their soul leaves the body, slips through cracks and keyholes and appears as a cat, straw or feather.

ekke-nekkepenn.depicted_variant: Christian Peter Hansen's North Sea merman variant
visual_requirements: Male North Frisian merman
Humanlike upper body merges into fish tail
North Sea seabed
Mischievous dangerous sea-spirit aura

basis_claims.quote: is a North Frisian legendary figure. In the middle of the 19th century, the local researcher, folklorist, and graphic artist Christian Peter Hansen ... portrayed Ekke Nekkepenn as a merman who lives with his wife Rahn at the bottom of the North Sea and plays mischievous tricks on seafarers and residents of the North Frisian Islands.

statement.id: Ekke Nekkepenn (juga Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 peneliti lokal, ahli folklor, dan seniman grafis Christian Peter Hansen menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki laut yang tinggal bersama istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk kepulauan Frisia Utara.
statement.en: Ekke Nekkepenn (also Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure; in the mid-19th century the local researcher, folklorist and artist Christian Peter Hansen portrayed him as a merman living with his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and playing tricks on seafarers and North Frisian islanders.

basis_claims.quote: Die Erzählung beginnt damit, dass Ekke Nekkepenn die Frau des Kapitäns eines im Sturm nach England laufenden Sylter Schiffes um Hilfe bei der Geburt seines Kindes bittet. Die schöne und hilfsbereite Kapitänsfrau wird vom Meermann zu seiner auf dem Grunde der Nordsee lebenden Frau Rahn geführt und kommt nach gelungener Geburt reichbeschenkt mit Gold und Silber an die Meeresoberfläche zurück.

statement.id: Kisahnya bermula ketika Ekke Nekkepenn meminta istri kapten kapal Sylt yang diterjang badai menuju Inggris membantu persalinan anaknya; perempuan itu dibawa ke istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan, setelah persalinan berhasil, kembali ke permukaan dengan hadiah emas dan perak.
statement.en: The tale begins with Ekke Nekkepenn asking the wife of the captain of a storm-tossed Sylt ship bound for England to help with his child's birth; she is led to his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and, after a successful birth, returns to the surface richly gifted with gold and silver.

basis_claims.quote: Several years later, Ekke Nekkepenn remembered this incident and decides – now that Rahn has become "old and wrinkly" – to take the captain's wife as his own. When he sees the Rantumer Captain's ship one day, he persuades Rahn, who's sitting on the seabed, to grind salt, and the resulting powerful vortex pulls down the Sylt ship

statement.id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian, karena Rahn telah "tua dan keriput", Ekke Nekkepenn ingin mengambil istri kapten itu; saat melihat kapal kapten dari Rantum, ia membujuk Rahn yang duduk di dasar laut untuk menggiling garam, dan pusaran kuat yang timbul menenggelamkan kapal Sylt itu.
statement.en: Years later, with Rahn now 'old and wrinkly', Ekke Nekkepenn decides to take the captain's wife; seeing the Rantum captain's ship, he gets Rahn on the seabed to grind salt, and the strong vortex pulls the Sylt ship down.

basis_claims.quote: Ekke Nekkepenn (på førfrisisk Eke Nekepen) er en nordfrisisk sagnfigur. Ifølge sagnet lever figuren sammen med sin kone Ran på bunden af Vesterhavet og driller søfarere og beboerne på de nordfrisiske øer. Han modsvarer på mange punkter Ægir. ... Stoffet blev også indarbejdet i Theodor Storms novelle Die Regentrude fra 1863.

statement.id: Ekke Nekkepenn (Frisia Föhr: Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara yang menurut sage tinggal bersama istrinya Ran di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk pulau; dalam banyak hal ia padanan Ægir, dan kisahnya juga diolah dalam novel Theodor Storm Die Regentrude dari 1863.
statement.en: Ekke Nekkepenn (Föhr Frisian Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure who by legend lives with his wife Ran on the North Sea floor teasing seafarers and islanders; he corresponds in many ways to Ægir, and the material was also worked into Theodor Storm's novella Die Regentrude of 1863.

nuckelavee.depicted_variant: Orcadian fused horse-and-human skinless sea demon
visual_requirements: Four finned horse legs
Exactly one centered horse eye
Hairless skinless horse fused with human upper torso
Two ground-reaching arms and frightening aura

basis_claims.quote: is a horse-like demon from Orcadian folklore that combines equine and human elements. If one was looking casually, or under the cover of shadow in the night, it was thought to have the silhouette of a normal horseman. However, upon further inspection, it resembles a fleshless horse which sports one eye and fins on its legs

statement.id: Nuckelavee iblis serupa kuda cerita rakyat Orkney (Orcadian folklore), tampak seperti penunggang kuda, tetapi kuda tanpa kulit bermata satu bersirip dengan tubuh manusia tanpa kulit di punggungnya.
statement.en: The nuckelavee is a horse-like demon of Orcadian folklore, seeming a horseman but a fleshless one-eyed finned horse with a fleshless human torso on its back.

basis_claims.quote: British folklorist Katharine Briggs called it "the nastiest" of all the demons of Scotland's Northern Isles.

statement.id: Folklorist Britania (British) Katharine Briggs menyebutnya yang paling keji di antara iblis Northern Isles Skotlandia (Scotland).
statement.en: British folklorist Katharine Briggs called it the nastiest of the demons of Scotland's Northern Isles.

basis_claims.quote: The nuckelavee's breath was thought to wilt crops and sicken livestock and the creature was held responsible for droughts and epidemics on land despite being predominantly a sea-dweller.

statement.id: Napas nuckelavee melayukan tanaman, menyakiti ternak, dan ia disalahkan atas kekeringan dan wabah meski hidup di laut.
statement.en: The nuckelavee's breath wilts crops and sickens livestock; it was blamed for droughts and epidemics though it lives in the sea.

basis_claims.quote: In common with many other sea monsters, it is unable to tolerate fresh water. Therefore, those it is pursuing have only to cross a river or stream to be rid of it.

statement.id: Seperti monster laut lain, ia tak tahan air tawar; orang yang dikejarnya cukup menyeberangi sungai.
statement.en: Like other sea monsters it cannot tolerate fresh water; those it chases need only cross a stream.

cat-sith.depicted_variant: Dog-sized large black fairy cat with white chest spot
visual_requirements: Dog-sized large black fairy cat with white chest spot

basis_claims.quote: is a fairy creature from Celtic mythology, said to resemble a large black cat with a white spot on its chest that walks on its hind legs. Legend has it that the spectral cat haunts the Scottish Highlands. The legends surrounding this creature are more common in Scottish folklore, but a few occur in Irish.

statement.id: Cat-sìth (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic; Irlandia, Irish cat sí) peri mitologi Kelt (Celtic), kucing hitam besar berbercak putih, berjalan dengan kaki belakang, di Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands); di Inggris Raya dan Irlandia. Lebih umum di Skotlandia (Scotland) daripada Irlandia (Ireland).
statement.en: The cat-sìth (Scottish Gaelic; Irish cat sí) is a fairy of Celtic myth, a large black cat with a white spot walking on its hind legs, in the Scottish Highlands. More common in Scotland than Ireland.

baobh-shith.depicted_variant: Green-clad fairy vampire with two clearly visible deer hooves
visual_requirements: Green-clad fairy vampire with two clearly visible deer hooves

basis_claims.quote: In a similar tale one of the men noticed that the women had deer hooves instead of feet and fled from them. He returned the next morning to find that the other hunters had their "throats cut and chests laid open".

statement.id: Para perempuan berkaki kuku rusa; kawan-kawannya ditemukan tergorok.
statement.en: The women had deer hooves; his companions were found with throats cut.

dobhar-chu.depicted_variant: Giant white otter-dog with black ear tips and black cross on back
visual_requirements: Giant white otter-dog with black ear tips and black cross on back

basis_claims.quote: The Dobhar-chú is described as resembling an otter, though about five times as large at 10–15 ft (3.0–4.6 m), with a white pelt, black ear tips, and a shape like a black cross on its back.

statement.id: Mirip berang-berang, lima kali lebih besar (3–4,6 m), berbulu putih, ujung telinga hitam, tanda salib hitam.
statement.en: Like an otter five times larger (3–4.6 m), white pelt, black ear tips, a black cross on its back.

twrch-trwyth.depicted_variant: Fabulous wild boar in Arthurian wilderness
visual_requirements: Fabulous wild boar in Arthurian wilderness

basis_claims.quote: is a fabulous wild boar in Arthurian legend. A richly elaborate account of its hunt is described in the Welsh prose romance Culhwch and Olwen, which was probably written around 1100. Its hunt involved King Arthur and his hosts and his hound Cafall

statement.id: Twrch Trwyth (Trwyd, Wales/Welsh) babi hutan legenda Arthurian; dalam Culhwch and Olwen (sekitar 1100) diburu Raja Arthur (King Arthur) dan anjing Cafall (Cavall); tugas raksasa Ysbaddaden.
statement.en: Twrch Trwyth (Welsh Trwyd) is a boar of Arthurian legend; in Culhwch and Olwen (c. 1100) hunted by King Arthur and his hound Cafall (Cavall); tasks set by the giant Ysbaddaden.

abasy.depicted_variant: Solitary abasy underworld monster without mount
visual_requirements: A hideous giant monster in a dark Sakha underworld cave, with exactly ONE central eye, ONE arm total on its right side and ONE thick leg total under the torso. Entire abnormal asymmetrical body visible; no second arm or leg and no hidden stumps. Jagged metallic iron teeth in the grimacing mouth. It balances on its sole leg; its lone claw-like hand reaches forward. No dragon, no rider, no horn.
Predatory and malevolent darkness
Creature-specific anatomy is clearly visible; no ordinary human dramatic portrait

basis_claims.quote: The abaasy occupy the lower level, referred to as the underworld or "kingdom of darkness."

statement.id: Abaasy menempati lapisan bawah alam semesta, yaitu dunia bawah atau "kerajaan kegelapan".
statement.en: The abaasy occupy the lower level of the universe, the underworld or "kingdom of darkness".

basis_claims.quote: The abbasy are described as "one-eyed, one-armed, one-legged" monsters mounted on "two-headed, eight-legged, two-tailed dragons as steeds."

statement.id: Abaasy digambarkan sebagai monster bermata satu, berlengan satu, dan berkaki satu yang menunggang naga berkepala dua, berkaki delapan, dan berekor dua.
statement.en: The abaasy are described as one-eyed, one-armed, one-legged monsters riding two-headed, eight-legged, two-tailed dragons.

basis_claims.quote: Es sind gigantische Wesen mit Zähnen aus Eisen und bewohnen im Weltbild der Jakuten die Unterwelt. Sie reisen in Gruppen von Sieben.

statement.id: Mereka makhluk raksasa bergigi besi yang menghuni dunia bawah dan bepergian dalam kelompok tujuh.
statement.en: They are giant beings with iron teeth who live in the underworld and travel in groups of seven.

visual_requirements: One immense intelligent bird of prey, raptor anatomy rather than lion hybrid, broad powerful wings, hooked beak, two taloned feet, fully feathered body. It stands alert above old Welsh moorland with commanding thoughtful gaze. No human, lion torso, harness, crown or costume.
Fierce obedient guardian intelligence
Creature-specific anatomy is clearly visible; no ordinary human dramatic portrait

basis_claims.quote: is a legendary creature from Welsh tradition depicted as very large and intelligent birds, often considered to be related to the griffin.

statement.id: Adar Llwch Gwin makhluk legenda tradisi Wales (Welsh), burung besar cerdas, kerabat griffin (Griffin); di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The Adar Llwch Gwin are legendary Welsh birds, very large and intelligent, related to the griffin.

basis_claims.quote: The name derives from the Welsh words adar ("bird"), llwch ("dust"), and gwin ("wine"). These birds were said to understand human speech and to obey whatever command was given to them by their master.

statement.id: Nama dari kata Wales (Welsh) adar burung, llwch debu, gwin anggur; paham bahasa manusia.
statement.en: The name is from Welsh adar bird, llwch dust, gwin wine; they understood human speech.

basis_claims.quote: Later, in medieval Welsh poetry, the phrase Adar Llwch Gwin came to describe all types of raptors including hawks, falcons, and brave men.

statement.id: Dalam puisi Wales abad pertengahan, frasa ini untuk burung pemangsa dan orang pemberani.
statement.en: In medieval Welsh poetry the phrase meant raptors and brave men.

adar-rhiannon.depicted_variant: Three magical singing birds of the Mabinogi
visual_requirements: Exactly THREE distinct magical birds perched on three branches over the Welsh coast at Harlech, three feathered avian bodies, separate heads and pairs of wings, beaks gently open in song.
