Elongated bent claw fingers, sharp teeth and distorted oni jaw clearly visible
Entire four-limb figure inside frame, nocturnal menacing temple-stalker aura
gagoze.aura: Menacing furtive nocturnal Gangō-ji temple demon

basis_claims.quote: Gagoze (元興寺), also gagoji, guwagoze, gangō, and gangōji no oni (元興寺の鬼, the oni of gangōji) is a yōkai said to have appeared at Gangō-ji in the Nara Prefecture around the Asuka period.

statement.id: Gagoze adalah yōkai yang konon menghantui Gangō-ji di Nara.
statement.en: Gagoze is a yōkai said to haunt Gangō-ji in Nara.

basis_claims.quote: In classical yōkai drawings such as the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien, it is depicted as an oni with the appearance of a monk.

statement.id: Ilustrasi lama menggambarkannya sebagai oni mirip biksu.
statement.en: Old illustrations portray it as an oni resembling a monk.

basis_claims.quote: He appears as a hideous demon dressed in monks robes, crawling about on all fours.

statement.id: Gambaran lain menyebut ia merangkak dengan empat anggota tubuh.
statement.en: Another description has it crawl on all fours.

nonhuman_features: Elongated bony claw hands and feet with hooked nails
Grotesque oni jaw and prominent sharp canine teeth
gagoze.historical_basis: Individually inspected Sekien's 1776 Gagoze plate (Commons scan of primary historical illustration): temple-eave crawling robed oni with distorted open-jawed face and very long claw fingers. Current research c03 identifies monk-like oni, c04 four-limb crawling. Retains source morphology without adding generic horns/wings.
artistic_changes: Painterly color, moonlit temple location and exact claw lengths interpreted from monochrome plate
Both hind feet made visible for four-limb review; no invented additional appendages

additional_sources.title: Gagoze in Gazu Hyakki Yagyo (1776)
additional_sources.author: Toriyama Sekien
additional_sources.publisher: Wikimedia Commons reproduction scanned from ISBN 4-336-03386-2
additional_sources.basis: Primary historical plate individually visually inspected for crawling clawed monk-robed oni morphology

additional_sources.title: Gazu Hyakki Yagyo
additional_sources.publisher: Tokyo University of the Arts Library
additional_sources.basis: 1776 original book catalog provenance

yaksha.depicted_variant: Silesaloma / Sticky-Hair forest-yakkha in Pañcāvudha Jataka #55
visual_requirements: One hawk beak and exactly two thick tusks
Disproportionately large head and bowl-like eyes
Shaggy coat, purple-mottled belly and blue-black palms

basis_claims.quote: In Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, the yakṣas have a dual personality. A yakṣa may be an inoffensive nature spirit associated with woods and mountains, or a darker version of the yakṣa which is a kind of Bhoota (ghost) that haunts the wilderness and waylays and devours travellers, similar to the rakṣasas.

statement.id: Versi yaksha dapat berupa roh alam yang tidak berbahaya atau hantu yang menghadang dan memangsa pelancong.
statement.en: A yaksha may be a harmless nature spirit or a ghost that waylays and devours travellers.

basis_claims.quote: In Buddhist literature, the yakṣa are the attendants of Vaiśravaṇa, the guardian of the northern quarter, a beneficent god who protects the righteous. The term also refers to the Twelve Heavenly Generals who guard Bhaiṣajyaguru, the Medicine Buddha. The yakshas of many Buddhist stories are ugly ogres, reborn in that form because of sins committed during their past lives as humans.

statement.id: Dalam literatur Buddhis, yaksha menjadi pengiring Vaisravana, penjaga arah utara.
statement.en: In Buddhist literature yakshas attend Vaisravana, guardian of the northern quarter.

nonhuman_features: One hawk beak and exactly two thick tusks
Disproportionately large head and bowl-like eyes
Shaggy coat, purple-mottled belly and blue-black palms
yaksha.historical_basis: Pañcāvudha Jataka #55 primary translation names Silesaloma a forest yakkha and gives specific nonhuman anatomy. This is one attested Buddhist yaksha subtype rather than a conflated Thai Ramakien guardian.
yaksha.artistic_changes: Stationary pose, forest lighting and modest waistcloth are interpretive; sole color follows prompt but soles are hidden by grounded stance.

additional_sources.title: Jataka 55: Pañcāvudha, translated by Robert Chalmers
additional_sources.purpose: Primary translated tale explicitly identifies this as a yakkha and describes broad head, bowl eyes, two tusks, hawk beak, purple-blotched belly, blue-black hands/feet and shaggy sticky coat.

lange-wapper.depicted_variant: Lange Wapper transformed entirely into a cat, as recorded by Domien Sleeckx (1840)
visual_requirements: One fully feline cat
One head, four separate legs/paws, one tail
Nighttime Antwerp context and taunting trickster pose
No human parts or invented hybrid anatomy
lange-wapper.aura: Knowing nocturnal obstruction and taunting mischief

basis_claims.quote: Lange Wapper is a Flemish folkloric character. He is a legendary giant and trickster whose folk tales were told especially in the city of Antwerp and its neighbouring towns, but similar tales are also prominent in other Flemish cities.

statement.id: Lange Wapper adalah tokoh cerita rakyat Flandria, raksasa legendaris dan penipu yang kisahnya terutama diceritakan di Antwerpen dan sekitarnya, meski kisah serupa juga menonjol di kota-kota Flandria lain.
statement.en: Lange Wapper is a Flemish folk character, a legendary giant and trickster whose tales were told especially in Antwerp and nearby towns, with similar tales prominent in other Flemish cities.

basis_claims.quote: Le Lange Wapper (en français, le Grand Wapper) est un géant de légende qui joue de mauvais tours aux habitants de la ville d'Anvers, en Belgique. Il apparaît la nuit et poursuit les gens qui ont trop bu. Il sait se faire très grand et très petit.

statement.id: Lange Wapper (Prancis: le Grand Wapper) adalah raksasa legenda yang mempermainkan warga Antwerpen, Belgia; ia muncul di malam hari, mengejar orang yang terlalu banyak minum, dan bisa membuat dirinya sangat besar atau sangat kecil.
statement.en: Lange Wapper (French le Grand Wapper) is a legendary giant who plays tricks on the people of Antwerp, Belgium; he appears at night, pursues those who drank too much, and can make himself very big or very small.

nonhuman_features: Entire feline transformation with cat muzzle, paws and tail
lange-wapper.historical_basis: Existing claims establish Antwerp nocturnal shapeshifting trickster. Sleeckx's historical primary tale explicitly supplies the selected cat form, distinct from related Kludde tales.
artistic_changes: Black coat, large cat proportions relative to alley, brick streetscape, lamp colours and side-on blocking pose are artistic choices, not fixed folklore characteristics.

additional_sources.title: Domien Sleeckx — De Lange Wapper (1840), Kronyken der straten van Antwerpen 3 (1843), p.154, DBNL
additional_sources.evidence: Original tale explicitly lists taking cat, dog or other animal shapes to frighten nighttime passers-by.

buschgro-mutter.depicted_variant: German Buschgroßmutter in recorded iron-headed ancient forest-spirit variant
visual_requirements: Whole bodily head and face of cold iron
Long tangled snow-white hair and staring eyes
buschgro-mutter.aura: Ambivalent stern ancient woodland guardian, eerie yet capable of reward

basis_claims.quote: is a legendary creature from German folklore, especially found in folktales from the regions Thuringia, Saxony, former German-speaking Silesia and the former German-speaking parts of Bohemia. She is called various regional names such as Pusch-Grohla ("shrub granny" in Silesian German) and Buschmutter ("shrub mother") in Silesia, 's Buschkathel ("th' Shrub-Katie") and Buschweibchen in Bohemia

statement.id: Buschgroßmutter ("nenek semak") adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Jerman (German), terutama di Thüringen (Thuringia), Sachsen (Saxony), Silesia, dan Bohemia, dengan nama daerah Pusch-Grohla dan Buschmutter di Silesia serta Buschweibchen di Bohemia.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter ('shrub grandmother') is a legendary creature of German folklore, especially in Thuringia, Saxony, Silesia and Bohemia, called Pusch-Grohla and Buschmutter in Silesia and Buschweibchen in Bohemia.

basis_claims.quote: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit living in the deepest woods which shows herself to humans only once every hundred years. She is as old as the hills, her appearance being small and ducked, wrinkly and ugly. She has staring eyes and is sometimes said to have an iron head, a typical demonic feature. The Buschgroßmutter's hair is long, as white as snow, but messy and full of lice.

statement.id: Buschgroßmutter adalah roh hutan di hutan terdalam yang menampakkan diri hanya sekali tiap seratus tahun; ia sangat tua, kecil, bungkuk, keriput, bermata melotot, berambut panjang seputih salju tetapi kusut dan berkutu.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit of the deepest woods, showing herself only once a century; ancient, small, stooped, wrinkled and staring, with long snow-white but tangled, lice-ridden hair.

basis_claims.quote: The character of the Buschgroßmutter is ambivalent, fluctuating between benevolent and malevolent behaviour. She asks people to comb or louse her hair. Those who fulfill her request will be rewarded with a neverending clew of yarn ... or with either green or yellow leaves which will later become gold if not thrown away.

statement.id: Watak Buschgroßmutter mendua antara baik dan jahat; ia meminta orang menyisir atau mencari kutu di rambutnya, dan yang memenuhinya diberi gulungan benang tak habis atau daun hijau atau kuning yang kelak menjadi emas bila tak dibuang.
statement.en: The Buschgroßmutter's character wavers between benevolent and malevolent; she asks people to comb or delouse her hair, and those who comply get an endless clew of yarn or green or yellow leaves that later become gold if kept.

basis_claims.quote: It is but very difficult to clean and tidy the Buschweibchen's hair because her head is as cold as ice, thus leading to a (temporary) freezing of the helper's hands. When she was sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the sneerer which will result in illnesses, most commonly rash.

statement.id: Merapikan rambutnya sangat sulit karena kepalanya sedingin es sehingga tangan penolong membeku sementara; bila diejek, Buschgroßmutter membalas dengan menghembuskan napas pada pengejek, yang lalu sakit, biasanya ruam kulit.
statement.en: Tidying her hair is very hard since her head is ice-cold, briefly freezing the helper's hands; when sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the mocker, who falls ill, usually with a rash.

nonhuman_features: Whole bodily head and face of cold iron
Long tangled snow-white hair and staring eyes
buschgro-mutter.historical_basis: Reviewed c02 explicitly says she is sometimes iron-headed and has tangled snow-white hair, staring eyes and stooped ancient form. c05 describes ice-cold head; c04 permits yarn-clew reward. Selected iron-head variant, no conflated Transylvanian traits.
buschgro-mutter.artistic_changes: Material texture, seated pose, cloth and yarn clew placement are interpretive ways to render sourced iron head and reward.

visual_requirements: Unmistakable large empty hollow opening in the back
Long dark hair with comb by a freshwater lake
Modest adult female form without unsupported added traits
One figure, complete seated silhouette
sjora.aura: Enigmatic lake guardian with restrained allure and storm-warning atmosphere

basis_claims.quote: The sjörå (in Swedish) , (lake Sjö) or the Sjöfru (Mistress of the Lake) was a mythical creature of the lake, or sjö, in Swedish folklore.

statement.id: Sjörå atau Sjöfru ("nyonya danau") adalah makhluk mitis danau dalam cerita rakyat Swedia (Swedish).
statement.en: The sjörå or Sjöfru ('Mistress of the Lake') was a mythical lake creature in Swedish folklore.

basis_claims.quote: She is a seductive creature, often featured sitting and combing her long, sweeping hair with delight, and often lures and drowns men who are unkind, unfaithful or otherwise disrespectful to her or the lake. Like all other rå (keepers) she protects her domain and awards those kind to her with prosperous fishing and good luck, by rescuing them from drowning and warning of incoming storms.

statement.id: Ia makhluk penggoda yang sering duduk menyisir rambut panjangnya dengan gembira, dan sering memikat serta menenggelamkan lelaki yang tidak ramah, tidak setia, atau tidak hormat kepadanya atau danau; seperti rå lain ia menjaga wilayahnya dan memberi yang baik kepadanya tangkapan melimpah, menyelamatkan dari tenggelam, dan memperingatkan badai.
statement.en: She is a seductive creature, often shown happily combing her long hair, who lures and drowns men unkind, unfaithful or disrespectful to her or the lake; like all rå she guards her domain and rewards the kind with good fishing, rescue from drowning and storm warnings.

basis_claims.quote: Sjörået är i nordisk folktro namnet på den ande eller rådare som vakar över en tjärn, en insjö eller – om det är ett mäktigt sjörå – över ett helt sjösystem.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik (nordisk), sjörå adalah nama roh atau penguasa yang menjaga telaga, danau, atau, bila sjörå itu kuat, seluruh sistem danau.
statement.en: In Nordic (nordisk) folk belief, the sjörå is the spirit or ruler watching over a pond, a lake or, if mighty, a whole lake system.

basis_claims.quote: Liksom skogsrået var hon en förförisk kvinnlig humanoid, som ibland kunde ha ihålig rygg eller vara delvis täckt med fjäll. ... För att undvika närkontakt med henne kunde man lätt skrämma bort henne med ett metallföremål. Ett sådant knep var att kasta fiskekniven framför hennes fötter och vips var hon försvunnen.

statement.id: Seperti skogsrå ia perempuan berwujud manusia yang menggoda, kadang berpunggung berongga atau sebagian bersisik; ia mudah diusir dengan benda logam, misalnya pisau ikan yang dilempar ke depan kakinya.
statement.en: Like the skogsrå she was a seductive humanlike female, sometimes hollow-backed or partly scaled; she was easily scared off with a metal object, such as a fishing knife thrown before her feet.

basis_claims.quote: Hon visade sig nästan enbart för ensamma män, som vistades i sjöns närhet, där hon med förtjusning brukade sitta på en sten och kamma sitt långa, mörka svepande hår.

statement.id: Ia menampakkan diri hampir hanya kepada lelaki sendirian di dekat danau, sambil duduk di batu dengan gembira menyisir rambut panjang gelapnya.
statement.en: She showed herself almost only to lone men near the lake, delightedly sitting on a stone combing her long dark hair.

nonhuman_features: Large visibly open hollow torso from upper back to lower back
sjora.historical_basis: Source claim sjora-c06 explicitly records hollow-backed or partly scaled alternatives; this selects hollow-backed alone. c03/c11 support combing long dark hair on a stone, guarding the lake and warning of storms.
artistic_changes: Cavity shape/inner shading, comb shape, cloth drape, rock, lake scenery and twilight colours are painterly choices. The exact appearance of the hollow interior is unspecified in the source.

gremlin.depicted_variant: Roald Dahl's 1942 bulbous-bodied, knobby-headed, stubby-horned aircraft gremlin
visual_requirements: Bulbous body, spindly legs and knobby round head
Two horns grown from head, not hat
Derby, red jacket, corduroys and suction boots
One tiny mechanical saboteur on an aircraft
gremlin.aura: Mischievous intent on tampering with aeroplane hardware

basis_claims.quote: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented at the beginning of the 20th century originally to explain malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes and their operators. Depictions of these creatures vary widely.

statement.id: Gremlin adalah makhluk usil rekaan dari awal abad ke-20 untuk menjelaskan kerusakan pesawat, lalu mesin lain; gambarannya beragam.
statement.en: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented in the early 20th century to explain aircraft and later machine malfunctions; depictions vary.

basis_claims.quote: Use of the term in the sense of a mischievous creature that sabotages aircraft first arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots stationed in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s, with the earliest printed record in a poem published in the journal Aeroplane in Malta on 10 April 1929.

statement.id: Kata gremlin untuk penyabotase pesawat muncul dalam slang Royal Air Force (RAF) di kalangan pilot Britania (British) di Malta, Middle East (Timur Tengah), dan India pada 1920-an; catatan tertua puisi di Aeroplane in Malta, 10 April 1929.
statement.en: The term for an aircraft saboteur arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s; earliest print a poem in Aeroplane in Malta, 10 April 1929.

nonhuman_features: Knobby round creature head with two short horns
Bulbous torso disproportionate to spindly legs
gremlin.historical_basis: Existing claims establish early RAF mechanical-sabotage gremlins. Additional museum source preserves Dahl's 1942 direct description supplying the selected structural anatomy and clothing.
artistic_changes: Olive knobby skin colouring, horn curvature, facial expression, crouch, screwdriver and hangar scene are painterly choices within Dahl's specified morphology.

additional_sources.title: The Walt Disney Family Museum — Roald Dahl, Author of Gremlins Book, Visits The Walt Disney Studios
additional_sources.evidence: Museum reproduces Dahl's contemporary description: bulbous body, spindly legs, knobby round head with stubby horns; derby, red jacket, corduroys, suction boots.

vor-r.depicted_variant: Vörr guardian spirit appearing as a small light, rather than its person's shape
visual_requirements: One modest light with no body or face
Old warden tree and farm context
Protective quiet aura, no threatening fiery monster
vor-r.aura: Quiet attentive protection beside a farm's old warden tree

basis_claims.quote: At times, the warden could reveal itself as a small light or as the shape of the person ... The perception of another person's warden could cause a physical sensation such as an itching hand or nose, as a foreboding or an apparition. The warden could arrive before the actual person ... The warden of a dead person could also become a revenant, haunting particular spots or individuals.

statement.id: Kadang penjaga menampakkan diri sebagai cahaya kecil atau sosok orangnya; merasakan penjaga orang lain bisa menimbulkan gatal di tangan atau hidung sebagai pertanda; penjaga bisa tiba sebelum orangnya, dan penjaga orang mati bisa menjadi hantu yang menghuni tempat atau orang tertentu.
statement.en: The warden might appear as a small light or in its person's shape; sensing another's warden could cause an itching hand or nose as a foreboding; it could arrive before the person, and a dead person's warden could become a revenant haunting places or people.

basis_claims.quote: A very old tree (often a linden, ash or elm) growing on the farm lot could be dubbed a "warden tree" (Danish: værnetræ ),(Swedish: vårdträd ), or (Norwegian: tuntre ) and was believed to defend it from bad luck. Breaking a leaf or twig from the warden tree was considered a serious offence.

statement.id: Pohon sangat tua (sering linden, ash, atau elm) di pekarangan dapat dijuluki "pohon penjaga" (Denmark: værnetræ; Swedia: vårdträd; Norwegia: tuntre) dan diyakini melindungi dari nasib buruk; mematahkan daun atau rantingnya dianggap pelanggaran berat.
statement.en: A very old tree (often linden, ash or elm) on the farm could be called a 'warden tree' (Danish værnetræ, Swedish vårdträd, Norwegian tuntre), believed to guard against bad luck; breaking its leaves or twigs was a serious offence.

basis_claims.quote: Un vörðr (del nórdico antiguo: cuidador o guardián) es un espíritu guardián en la mitología nórdica, que se supone sigue desde el nacimiento hasta la muerte el alma (hugr) de cada persona.

statement.id: Vörðr (Nordik Kuno, "pemelihara" atau "penjaga"; juga ditulis vǫrðr) adalah roh penjaga dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini mengikuti jiwa (hugr) setiap orang sejak lahir sampai mati.
statement.en: A vörðr (Old Norse 'caretaker' or 'guardian') is a guardian spirit of Norse mythology believed to follow each person's soul (hugr) from birth to death.

nonhuman_features: Entirely luminous presence without humanoid silhouette or animal anatomy
vor-r.historical_basis: Claim c02 records the guardian appearing as a small light; c03 records old trees on farms as warden trees; c04 identifies lifelong guardian association.
artistic_changes: Amber light colour, tree bark/leaf details, Norwegian-style farm, moonlight and mountain view are aesthetic choices. Tree species is unspecified visually and not asserted to be ash.

yurei.depicted_variant: Footless Yūrei apparition in Japanese ghost art and literature
visual_requirements: Two arms with dangling hands
Long black hair and white burial kimono
Footless form ends in one narrow spectral taper suspended clear of the ground

basis_claims.quote: Generally speaking, a yūrei is the spirit of a person who has died, usually appearing as they did in life.

statement.id: Yūrei adalah roh seseorang yang sudah meninggal.
statement.en: Yūrei is the spirit of a deceased person.

basis_claims.quote: Yūrei refers to the spirits of humans who do not cross over to the other side and remain in the human world for personal reasons or because the funeral or burial rites were not sufficient or satisfactory.

statement.id: Yūrei dapat tinggal di dunia manusia karena alasan pribadi atau upacara pemakaman yang kurang memadai.
statement.en: Yūrei may remain in the human world for personal reasons or insufficient funeral rites.

basis_claims.quote: The typical yūrei, as depicted in art and literature, is described as a woman with long, disheveled black hair obstructing the face, wearing burial clothing, with curved dangling hands and no feet.

statement.id: Dalam seni dan sastra, yūrei lazim digambarkan sebagai perempuan berambut hitam panjang, berpakaian pemakaman, bertangan menggantung, dan tanpa kaki.
statement.en: In art and literature yūrei are often shown as long-haired women in burial clothes, with dangling hands and no feet.

nonhuman_features: Complete absence of feet and lower legs in visibly tapering airborne ghost form
yurei.historical_basis: Reviewed yurei-c04 records typical artistic iconography: long black hair, burial clothing, curved dangling hands and no feet, based on BYU Library Bakemono source.
yurei.artistic_changes: Moonlit cemetery composition and smooth spectral taper are artistic treatments of documented footlessness.

swan-maiden.depicted_variant: Whole-swan transformation in Herman Hofberg's Blekinge Swan Maiden tale (1890)
visual_requirements: Whole natural swan body with one head, two wings and two separate webbed feet
No human face, human torso, invented hybrid anatomy, costume or crown
Entire swan uncropped with wistful graceful otherworldly aura
swan-maiden.aura: Graceful wistful supernatural freedom, quiet fairy-tale melancholy

basis_claims.quote: This is a study of the meaning of gender as framed by the swan maiden tale, a story found in the folklore of virtually every culture.

statement.id: Kisah Swan Maiden memiliki sebaran lintas budaya.
statement.en: The Swan Maiden story is found across many cultures.

basis_claims.quote: When she manages to regain this key, she escapes to the otherworld, never to return.

statement.id: Ketika mendapatkan kembali benda yang membebaskannya, ia pergi ke dunia lain.
statement.en: When she recovers that key, she escapes to another world.

nonhuman_features: Wholly avian swan metamorphosis, not a woman in feather clothing
swan-maiden.historical_basis: Herman Hofberg, Swedish Fairy Tales, translated W. H. Myers (1890), pp.35–38, Blekinge tale, transcribed by University of Pittsburgh D.L. Ashliman: swans divest feathers and become maidens, recover former shape and fly; youngest explicitly transforms back into a swan on recovering feathers. Selects this actual animal variant rather than Jacobs's feather-robed human account.
artistic_changes: Exact bill coloring, pose and Scandinavian lakeshore painterly details interpreted; no invented anatomy

additional_sources.title: Swan Maidens: The Swan Maiden (Sweden, Herman Hofberg)
additional_sources.publisher: University of Pittsburgh, D. L. Ashliman
additional_sources.basis: Hofberg 1890 pp.35–38, Blekinge tale; explicit complete swan transformation

bysen.depicted_variant: Bysen appearing as an inconspicuous tree stump in Gotland folklore
visual_requirements: One entirely stump-shaped subject
No human face or body, hat or axe on stump
Grey weathered stump, roots and woodland context
Mischievous forest/landmark context without added anatomy
bysen.aura: Hidden woodland mischief suggested by forked trails, boundary stone and timber transport setting

basis_claims.quote: Bysen är i gotländsk folktro ett litet skogsväsen som lockar människor att gå vilse eller ställer till förtret för skogsarbetarna.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Gotland (Swedia), Bysen adalah makhluk hutan kecil yang memikat orang tersesat atau menyusahkan pekerja hutan.
statement.en: In the folk belief of Gotland (Sweden), Bysen is a small forest being who lures people astray or causes trouble for forest workers.

basis_claims.quote: Bysen försenar också transporter och välter timmerlass. Han uppträder ofta som stubbe eller en liten grå, oansenlig gubbe, och beskylls för allt möjligt ofog.

statement.id: Bysen menunda pengangkutan dan menjungkirkan muatan kayu; ia sering muncul sebagai tunggul atau lelaki tua kelabu kecil yang tak mencolok, dan dituduh atas segala kenakalan.
statement.en: Bysen also delays transports and tips over timber loads; he often appears as a stump or a small, insignificant grey old man and is blamed for all sorts of mischief.

basis_claims.quote: Bysar är avlidna människor, enligt somliga källor, som lurat till sig någon annans mark genom att flytta de råmärken som markerade gränsen mellan två ägor. Som straff får de ingen ro i graven

statement.id: Menurut sebagian sumber, bysar adalah orang mati yang merebut tanah orang lain dengan memindahkan patok batas antara dua bidang tanah; sebagai hukuman mereka tak tenang di kubur.
statement.en: According to some sources, bysar are dead people who tricked others out of land by moving the markers between two holdings; as punishment they get no rest in the grave.

basis_claims.quote: Om en människa går efter Bysen och flyttar tillbaka de orätta gränsmärkena till rätt ställe, då får Bysen frid. På det svenska fastlandet kallas motsvarigheten skälvrängare

statement.id: Bila seseorang mengikuti Bysen dan mengembalikan patok yang salah ke tempatnya, Bysen mendapat damai; di daratan Swedia (svenska) padanannya disebut skälvrängare atau osaliga lantmätare, sementara mereka bergumam "Här är rätt, här är orätt".
statement.en: If someone follows Bysen and moves the wrong markers back, Bysen finds peace; on the Swedish (svenska) mainland the counterpart is called skälvrängare or osaliga lantmätare, and they mutter 'Här är rätt, här är orätt'.

basis_claims.quote: Den som Bysen får syn på i skogen, får synen förvrängd, så att denne inte kan hitta hem igen. Den som drabbas kan, genom att vända ett plagg ut och in, återfå normal syn.

statement.id: Siapa pun yang terlihat oleh Bysen di hutan menjadi kacau penglihatannya sehingga tak bisa pulang; ia dapat memulihkannya dengan membalik pakaian.
statement.en: Whoever Bysen sees in the forest has their sight twisted so they cannot find home; turning a garment inside out restores normal sight.

nonhuman_features: Entire tree-stump manifestation without human or animal anatomy
bysen.historical_basis: Claim c02 explicitly records Bysen appearing as a stump; c01/c06 describe leading people astray and forestry trouble; c04/c05 describe disputed boundary stones.
artistic_changes: Stump dimensions, generic tree species, forest layout, timber pile, grey bark/lichen and moonlighting are aesthetic choices. No supernatural anatomy added; the scene presents the plain-looking recorded stump form.

feuermann-ghost.depicted_variant: German Feuermann fiery ghost in the recorded snake manifestation
visual_requirements: One continuous limbless snake body with one head and tapering tail
Fire surrounds the snake silhouette
No humanoid body or invented hybrid anatomy
Nocturnal wet field boundary setting
feuermann-ghost.aura: Eerie nocturnal wandering and a fiery presence at a field boundary

basis_claims.quote: is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small.

statement.id: Feuermann ("manusia api"; juga Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) adalah hantu berapi dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German) yang berbeda dari will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) karena ukurannya: Feuermänner agak besar, Irrlichter agak kecil.
statement.en: The Feuermann ('fire man'; also Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) is a fiery ghost of German folklore, unlike the will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) in size: Feuermänner are big, Irrlichter small.

basis_claims.quote: Alternatively, the Feuermann also appears more or less shapeless like a (sometimes gigantic) sheaf or bundle of straw, a big floating light, a fiery ball, a pyramid, a snake, or a fiery wheel. The Feuermann is very quick and able to rise in the air so that it hovers above the treetops.

statement.id: Feuermann juga bisa tampil hampir tanpa bentuk, seperti berkas jerami (kadang raksasa), cahaya besar melayang, bola api, piramida, ular, atau roda api; ia sangat cepat dan dapat naik ke udara melayang di atas pucuk pohon.
statement.en: The Feuermann may also appear nearly shapeless, as a (sometimes giant) sheaf of straw, a big floating light, a fireball, a pyramid, a snake or a fiery wheel; it is very fast and can rise to hover above the treetops.

basis_claims.quote: It is seen as a sinner remaining hauntingly on earth to repent for its sins during lifetime. Frequently, the Feuermann is a so-called Grenzfrevler (sg., pl.) or boundary sinner who has moved a boundary stone or similar landmark with criminal intent, thus damning the soul to haunt the very boundary it unlawfully changed in life.

statement.id: Feuermann dianggap pendosa yang bergentayangan di bumi untuk menebus dosa semasa hidup; sering ia seorang Grenzfrevler yang memindahkan batu batas dengan niat jahat sehingga jiwanya dikutuk menghantui batas itu.
statement.en: The Feuermann is seen as a sinner haunting the earth to atone for its life's sins; often a Grenzfrevler who moved a boundary stone with criminal intent and is damned to haunt that boundary.

basis_claims.quote: The Feuermann appears only at evening or at night, preferably at fields, particularly field borders, and meadows, especially swampy ones.

statement.id: Feuermann hanya muncul pada sore atau malam hari, terutama di ladang, khususnya batas ladang, dan padang rumput, terutama yang berawa.
statement.en: The Feuermann appears only in the evening or at night, preferably in fields, especially field borders, and meadows, particularly swampy ones.

nonhuman_features: Fully serpentine body formed from supernatural fire, no human parts
feuermann-ghost.historical_basis: Verified research claim c03 records snake and fiery-wheel alternatives plus floating flight; c05 records nocturnal field boundaries and wet meadows.
artistic_changes: Generic snake species, curving pose, orange-gold fire, moonlit composition and boundary stone details are artistic choices.

baba-yaga.depicted_variant: Baba Yaga with an extraordinarily long literal iron nose and sharp iron teeth, recorded by Ralston
visual_requirements: Long literal iron nose anatomically continuous with face
Sharp iron teeth
One gaunt elderly hag, two arms/hands and two legs/feet
Source-compatible hut, mortar, pestle and broom
baba-yaga.aura: Formidable knowing forest tester, threatening and ambiguous

basis_claims.quote: Baba Yaga (Baba Jaga) is a witch or ogress from Slavic folklore who lives in a magical hut in the forest and either helps, imprisons, or eats people (usually children).

statement.id: Baba Yaga adalah penyihir atau raksasa perempuan dari folklor Slavia yang tinggal di gubuk ajaib di hutan dan membantu atau memangsa manusia.
statement.en: Baba Yaga is a witch or ogress from Slavic folklore who lives in a magical hut in the forest and either helps, imprisons, or eats people.

basis_claims.quote: built on four tall chicken legs that can turn about or relocate on command. She is often seen draped over her stove or reclining in the hut across the entire expanse, with her large nose touching the ceiling.

statement.id: Gubuk Baba Yaga berdiri di atas empat kaki ayam tinggi yang dapat berputar atau berpindah tempat sesuai perintah, dengan hidung besarnya menyentuh langit-langit.
statement.en: Baba Yaga hut is built on four tall chicken legs that can turn about or relocate on command, with her large nose touching the ceiling.

basis_claims.quote: she rides in a mortar propelled by a pestle with one hand while, in the other, she holds a broom she uses to wipe away any trace of her tracks. Baba Yaga can generally be understood to mean "Grandmother Witch"

statement.id: Baba Yaga terbang mengendarai lesung kayu yang didorong alu dengan satu tangan, sementara tangan lainnya memegang sapu untuk menghapus jejaknya.
statement.en: Baba Yaga rides in a mortar propelled by a pestle with one hand while holding a broom in the other to wipe away traces of her tracks.

basis_claims.quote: According to folklore, Baba Yaga is a supernatural crone who lives deep in the Russian forest, in a house perched on chicken feet and surrounded by pine trees and glowing skulls.

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, Baba Yaga adalah perempuan tua supernatural yang tinggal jauh di dalam hutan Rusia di rumah berkaki ayam yang dikelilingi pohon pinus dan tengkorak bercahaya.
statement.en: According to folklore, Baba Yaga is a supernatural crone living deep in the Russian forest in a house on chicken feet surrounded by pine trees and glowing skulls.

basis_claims.quote: Protruding from the top of a wooden mortar, the old crone squats, her thin lips as downcast as her dark eyes.

statement.id: Bermunculan dari lesung kayu, wanita tua ini berjongkok dengan bibir tipis terkatup dan mata gelap.
statement.en: Protruding from a wooden mortar, the old crone squats with thin downcast lips and dark eyes.

nonhuman_features: Exceptionally elongated literal metal nose
Sharp metal tooth row
baba-yaga.historical_basis: Ralston's historical folklore accounts expressly provide iron nasal and dental anatomy. The familiar bony-leg epithet was not interpreted as an exposed skeleton.
artistic_changes: Exact nose length/curve, hammered metal texture, seated porch pose, tool arrangement and dress/lighting are aesthetic interpretation of the recorded iron-nose form. A small chicken-legged hut in the distance is setting, not a replacement for Baba Yaga.

additional_sources.title: W.R.S. Ralston (1873) — Russian Fairy Tales, p.147
additional_sources.evidence: Primary collection describes tall gaunt dishevelled Baba Yaga, sometimes with a long iron nose reaching through the ceiling.

additional_sources.title: W.R.S. Ralston (1872) — Songs of the Russian People, p.161
additional_sources.evidence: The archived original additionally records the nose and strong sharp teeth sometimes being iron.

fish-man.depicted_variant: Liérganes Fish-Man in his early sea-return folkloric form with front scale strip and apparent neck gills
visual_requirements: Humanlike body with unmistakable anatomical fish-scale strip from throat to belly
Apparent gill openings on neck
Pale skin and short red hair
No tail, fins or other unsupported hybrid traits
fish-man.aura: Withdrawn distant seaborne presence of the returned amphibious figure

basis_claims.quote: The fish-man of Liérganes (Spanish: El hombre pez) is an entity of the mythology of Cantabria, located in the north of Spain. The fish-man would be an amphibian human-looking being, who looked a lot like a metamorphosis of a real human being who was lost at sea.

statement.id: Manusia ikan Liérganes (El hombre pez) adalah sosok mitologi Cantabria, makhluk amfibi berwujud manusia yang tampak seperti hasil perubahan seorang manusia nyata yang hilang di laut.
statement.en: The fish-man of Liérganes (El hombre pez) is a figure of Cantabrian mythology, an amphibious humanlike being that seemed the transformation of a real man lost at sea.

basis_claims.quote: However, five years later, in 1679, while some fishers were seafaring in the Bay of Cadiz, in southern Spain, they noticed that a strange-looking creature had become entangled with their fishing nets, and was trying to fight its way out.

statement.id: Lima tahun kemudian, pada 1679, nelayan di Teluk Cádiz melihat makhluk aneh tersangkut di jaring mereka dan berusaha meloloskan diri.
statement.en: Five years later, in 1679, fishermen in the Bay of Cádiz saw a strange creature caught in their nets, struggling to escape.

basis_claims.quote: When they got the creature on board, they found that it had indeed a human shape: it looked like a young man, with white skin and thin red hair. However, he also showed some fish-like signs, such as a strip of scales that went down from his throat to his stomach, another one that covered his spine, and what seemingly were gills around his neck.

statement.id: Setelah ditangkap dengan umpan roti, makhluk itu ternyata berwujud pemuda berkulit putih berambut merah tipis, tetapi bersisik dari leher sampai perut dan di sepanjang tulang punggung, serta tampak berinsang di lehernya.
statement.en: Once caught with bread, the creature proved to be a young man with white skin and thin red hair, but with a strip of scales from throat to belly and down his spine, and what looked like gills on his neck.

nonhuman_features: Overlapping scale strip anatomically continuous along front torso
Recessed apparent gill slits on both neck sides
fish-man.historical_basis: Verified research fish-man-c06 supplies scale strip and apparent neck gills; Feijoo §II.15 independently records early scales and explains their later disappearance. This depicts the legendary early form, not historical biological truth.
artistic_changes: Exact scale colour, strip width, gill slit count/depth, cloth and coastal stance/lighting are visual interpretations of the record. No additional piscine appendages.

additional_sources.title: Benito Jerónimo Feijoo — Teatro crítico universal VI, Discurso VIII, §II.15
additional_sources.evidence: Primary account reconciles reports denying later scales with early-arrival reports of a spine patch and strip from throat to stomach. It does not independently supply gills.

ghillie-dhu.depicted_variant: Contemporary Scottish educational retelling with seasonal green skin
visual_requirements: Naturally green skin on face, hands, arms and bare feet
Black hair and dark brown eyes
Woven moss/leaves clothes and solitary birch-wood habitat

basis_claims.quote: is a solitary male fairy described in Scottish folklore. He was said to be dark-haired, and clothed in leaves and moss, from which the ghillie suit got its name. He appears primarily in accounts from the late 18th century, living in a birch wood in the north-west Highlands of Scotland.

statement.id: Ghillie Dhu (Gille Dubh), peri lelaki penyendiri folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Scotland), rambut gelap, berpakaian daun dan lumut, asal nama ghillie suit; akhir abad ke-18; hutan birch Dataran Tinggi (Highlands) barat laut; menjaga hutan, baik kepada anak.
statement.en: Ghillie Dhu (Gille Dubh), a solitary male fairy of Scottish folklore, dark-haired, clothed in leaves and moss, origin of the ghillie suit; late 18th century; birch wood in the north-west Highlands; guards the forest, kind to children.

basis_claims.quote: He was said to live in the birch woods near Loch an Draing, in the north-west Highland area of Gairloch.

statement.id: Hutan birch dekat Loch an Draing, Gairloch; Katharine Briggs: roh gunung lembut, pemalu, liar, kecil.
statement.en: Birch woods near Loch an Draing, Gairloch; Katharine Briggs: gentle mountain spirit, timid, wild, small.

basis_claims.quote: The best known account of the Ghillie Dhu involves a girl named Jessie Macrae, who lived near the woods. She wandered into the woods and became lost as the sun went down.

statement.id: Jessie Macrae tersesat; Ghillie Dhu menghibur dan mengantarnya pulang.
statement.en: Jessie Macrae got lost; the Ghillie Dhu comforted her and led her home.

nonhuman_features: Green seasonal skin throughout face and bare limbs distinct from leafy costume
ghillie-dhu.historical_basis: Reviewed original folklore supplies solitary dark-haired leafy-clothed Gairloch birch fairy. School-hosted later educational retelling adds seasonal green skin; image explicitly selects that contemporary retelling and does not backdate skin detail.
ghillie-dhu.artistic_changes: Spring green phase, degree of green saturation, woven clothing shape and lake viewpoint are illustrative choices; modern retelling attributes skin colouring itself.

additional_sources.title: Carstairs Primary School: Scottish Myths and Legends Fact File
additional_sources.locator: PDF p7 of8 Ghillie Dhu; downloaded and text extracted
additional_sources.purpose: Educational retelling explicitly states green-to-brown seasonal skin, black hair, dark-brown eyes, leafy/moss clothes and one-metre stature. This later retelling is identified, not claimed as earliest folklore.

yuki-onna.depicted_variant: Akita one-legged smooth-faced Yuki-onna, Fujisawa1928 record
visual_requirements: Completely smooth blank face with no features or mask seams
One central leg and one visible bare foot
Two coherent hands and wintry white kimono appearance
yuki-onna.aura: Quiet uncanny snow apparition in dark mountain woodland

basis_claims.quote: The Yuki Onna is one of Japan’s most well-known and yet unknown yokai. There is no single story of the Yuki Onna.

statement.id: Yuki-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang tidak mempunyai satu kisah tunggal.
statement.en: Yuki-onna is a Japanese yōkai without a single definitive story.

basis_claims.quote: Anywhere there is ice and snow in Japan you will find legends of the Yuki Onna, often called by some regional variation.

statement.id: Cerita Yuki-onna terdapat di daerah Jepang yang bersalju dan memiliki variasi daerah.
statement.en: Yuki-onna stories occur in snowy parts of Japan and have regional variants.

basis_claims.quote: She resembles a classic yurei, with snow-white skin and a white kimono. The kimono is usually described as a thin, summer kimono
basis_claims.locator: What Do Yuki Onna Look Like?

statement.id: Yuki-onna kerap digambarkan berkulit putih dan mengenakan kimono putih.
statement.en: Yuki-onna is often depicted with white skin and a white kimono.

nonhuman_features: Featureless face without eyes, nose or mouth
One central leg/foot characteristic of the selected Akita account

hag.historical_basis: Generic hag current research describes old witch/fairy supernatural class (c01/c05/c06/c07). Selects a specifically identified member of that class, Black Annis, as regional exemplar. Leicester City Council's original heritage service directly records blue features and quotes John Heyrick's 1797 On a Cave Called Black Annis's Bower describing vast talons instead of hands. University of Vienna folklore study identifies Black Annis as old hag and quotes Briggs on sharp teeth, long black claws and blue face. Does not transfer this anatomy to all hags, equate it with all goddesses, or claim extra horns/animal body.
artistic_changes: Named regional hag exemplar used for generic class entry, explicitly limited in depicted_variant
Exact claw curvature/blue shade/cave staging and rough opaque dress interpreted; human-skin garments avoided

amaterasu.historical_basis: Uses an Ise-related historical snake-deity interpretation documented in primary scholarly research, not a mirror symbol, game wolf or dragon-fox hybrid. The medieval diary's unknown exact form remains an acknowledged limitation.
artistic_changes: Gold/cream colouring, snake species/scale pattern, exact size and pose, cedar grove, sunrise and distant shrine architecture are artistic choices. Source does not specify these details; no claim that this replaces common human Amaterasu iconography.

Matsumae discusses Tsūkai Sankeiki, Zoku Gunsho-ruijū70, whose Ise story mentions snake/lizard-like scales but says only the priestess knew the form. The image selects this scholarly snake-deity interpretation without claiming the diary definitively names a snake species.

aos-si.depicted_variant: Scottish Gaelic Sìth woman transformed entirely into a red-deer hind

basis_claims.quote: The term aos sí means "folk of the sí"; these are the mounds in which they are said to dwell, which are seen as portals to an Otherworld. Such abodes are referred to in English as "shees", "fairy mounds", "elf mounds" or "hollow hills". The aos sí interact with humans and the human world. They are variously said to be the ancestors, the spirits of nature, or goddesses and gods.

statement.id: Aos sí berarti bangsa sí, gundukan gerbang ke Dunia Lain (Otherworld), dalam bahasa Inggris (English) fairy mounds atau hollow hills; mereka disebut leluhur, roh alam, atau dewa-dewi.
statement.en: Aos sí means folk of the sí, mounds that are portals to an Otherworld, in English fairy mounds or hollow hills; they are called ancestors, nature spirits, or gods.

basis_claims.quote: adalah istilah yang mengacu kepada ras supranatural dalam mitologi Irlandia dan Skotlandia yang mirip dengan peri atau elf. artistic_changes: One antlerless adult hind is selected; reddish coat, stance, mound opening and Highland sunset/mist are composition choices within the red-deer manifestation.

additional_sources.title: John Gregorson Campbell (1900) — Superstitions of Highlands and Islands, pp.28 and50
additional_sources.evidence: Primary oral-folklore collection explicitly describes Sìth fairy women assuming red-deer shapes. This selects a Scottish manifestation, not all Aos sí.

They are referred to as Shivaganas or Rudraganas and Rudraganikas are considered the female equivalents.

statement.en: Ganas in Hindu mythological context are Shiva's attendants living on Kailash.

statement.en: A pixie (pisky, pixy, piskie or pigsie in Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

batibat.depicted_variant: Ilocano ancient corpulent female tree-post nightmare spirit

Rough timber house support post

basis_claims.quote: The Batibat is a vengeful demon found in Ilocano folklore. In Tagalog folklore, the creature is called Bangungot. The batibat takes the form of an ancient, grotesquely obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

statement.id: Batibat adalah setan pendendam dalam cerita rakyat Ilokano, disebut bangungot dalam cerita rakyat Tagalog, berwujud roh perempuan tua yang sangat gemuk penghuni pohon.
statement.en: The batibat is a vengeful demon of Ilocano folklore, called bangungot in Tagalog folklore, taking the form of an ancient, grossly obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

basis_claims.quote: They usually come in contact with humans when the trees in which they reside are felled and are made homeless, especially when their tree is made into a support post for a house.

statement.id: Batibat biasanya bersentuhan dengan manusia ketika pohonnya ditebang, terutama bila dijadikan tiang rumah, lalu ia menghuni sisa pohonnya.
statement.en: Batibat usually meet humans when their trees are felled, especially when made into a house post, and then inhabit what is left of the tree.

basis_claims.quote: When a person does sleep near it, the batibat transforms into its true form and attacks the person by suffocating their victim and invading their dream space, causing sleep paralysis and waking nightmares. This condition lends itself to the Ilocano word for nightmare, "batíbat"

statement.id: Batibat melarang manusia tidur di dekat tiangnya; bila ada yang tidur di sana, ia berubah ke wujud aslinya, menindih korban dan memasuki mimpinya hingga terjadi ketindihan dan mimpi buruk; dari sinilah kata Ilokano batíbat untuk mimpi buruk.
statement.en: The batibat forbids sleeping near its post; if someone does, it takes its true form, smothers the victim and invades their dreams, causing sleep paralysis and nightmares; hence the Ilocano word batíbat for nightmare.

nonhuman_features: Aged extremely corpulent female spirit associated with her felled tree's house post and nightmare attacks; no anatomical deformation claimed
batibat.historical_basis: Ilocano folklore describes an ancient very obese woman-shaped tree spirit that moves into a support post made from her tree and induces nightmares near it. Retains source-described human female anatomy without added monster traits.

knocker-folklore.aura: One tiny approximately two-foot tall human-shaped Cornish mining spirit in humble old working clothes and cloth cap, wrinkled male face, normal rounded ears, knocking on a dark tin-mine rock wall with a small mining hammer. One other hand holds a simple candle whose warm light reveals mineral veins. Broad mine passage and tool size establish tiny scale. Solemn uncanny warning of mine collapse in damp subterranean darkness, no collapsed victims, no modern equipment.

basis_claims.quote: The Knocker, Knacker, or Tommyknocker (US) is a mythical, subterranean, gnome-like creature in Cornish and Devon folklore. The Welsh counterpart is the coblyn. It is closely related to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker and the English and Scottish brownie. The Cornish describe the creature as a little person 2 ft 0 in (0.61 m) tall

statement.id: Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker, AS) makhluk bawah tanah mirip gnome cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish) dan Devon; Wales (Welsh) coblyn; kerabat leprechaun Irlandia (Irish), kloker Kent (Kentish), brownie Inggris dan Skotlandia (English and Scottish); 61 cm; usil mencuri perkakas (Coblyn, Leprechaun, Brownie); di Britania dan AS.
statement.en: The Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker) is a subterranean gnome-like creature of Cornish and Devon folklore; Welsh coblyn; kin to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker, English and Scottish brownie; 0.61 m tall.

basis_claims.quote: Cornish miners believed that the diminutive Knockers beckoned them toward finding rich veins of tin. As miners changed from independent, family-owned operators to hired laborers for large industrialized companies, there was an increased concern for safety, reflected in the knockers' new role. They knocked on the mine walls to warn of impending collapse.

statement.id: Penambang Cornwall (Cornish): knocker menuntun ke urat timah, mengetuk untuk memperingatkan runtuhan.
statement.en: Cornish miners: knockers led them to tin and knocked to warn of collapse.

basis_claims.quote: Generally considered benevolent, they were also tricksters who would hide tools and extinguish candles. They are similar to the coblynau of Welsh miners.

statement.id: Umumnya baik, tetapi usil: menyembunyikan perkakas, memadamkan lilin; mirip coblynau Wales (Welsh).

basis_claims.quote: are a class of fairy-folk, variously compared to dwarfs, elves, or spirits, described in German folklore as having an intimate connection to trees and the forest.

statement.id: Orang lumut (Moosleute), juga orang kayu (Holzleute) atau orang hutan (Waldleute), adalah golongan peri yang dibandingkan dengan kurcaci, elf, atau roh, digambarkan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German) memiliki ikatan erat dengan pohon dan hutan.
statement.en: Moss people (Moosleute), also wood folk (Holzleute) or forest folk (Waldleute), are a class of fairy-folk compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits, described in German folklore as intimately tied to trees and the forest.

basis_claims.quote: The moss people are sometimes described as similar to dwarfs, being the same size as children, but "grey and old-looking, hairy, and clad in moss." Sometimes, moss folk are also bigger. In other descriptions they are said to be pretty.

statement.id: Orang lumut kadang digambarkan mirip kurcaci, sebesar anak-anak, tetapi kelabu, tampak tua, berbulu, dan berbalut lumut; kadang lebih besar, dan dalam deskripsi lain cantik.
statement.en: Moss people are sometimes like dwarfs, child-sized but grey, old-looking, hairy and moss-clad; sometimes bigger, and in other accounts pretty.

basis_claims.quote: Moss people, especially the females of the species, are able to send plagues on one hand; on the other, they can also heal the victims of such plagues. During epidemics the Holzfräulein ("Wood ladies") would emerge from the forest to show the people which medicinal herbs could cure or ward off plague.

statement.id: Orang lumut, terutama yang perempuan, dapat mendatangkan wabah tetapi juga menyembuhkan korbannya; saat epidemi Holzfräulein keluar dari hutan untuk menunjukkan tanaman obat penyembuh atau penangkal wabah.
statement.en: Moss people, especially females, can send plagues yet also heal their victims; in epidemics the Holzfräulein came out of the forest to show which herbs cure or prevent plague.

basis_claims.quote: Die Moosweiblein leben im Wald. Sie wohnen auf der Heide, an dunklen Orten im Holz oder im tiefsten Wald. Ihre Behausung ist ein Erdloch, ein hohler Baum, ein Häuslein aus Baumwurzeln oder eine Mooshütte. Sie schlafen auf Moos und betten auch ihre Kinder auf Moos oder Rinde.

statement.id: Moosweiblein tinggal di hutan, di padang, di tempat gelap, atau di hutan terdalam; rumahnya rongga tanah, pohon berlubang, pondok dari akar, atau pondok lumut; mereka tidur di atas lumut dan membaringkan anak-anaknya di atas lumut atau kulit kayu.
statement.en: Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; child-sized grey hairy old forest spirit wearing moss garments, associated with trees and healing herbs.

basis_claims.quote: A gandharva (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व) is a member of a class of celestial beings in Indian religions, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, whose males are divine performers such as musicians and singers, and the females are divine dancers. In Hinduism, they are regarded to be the celestial demigods who serve as the musicians of the devas.

statement.id: Gandharva adalah golongan makhluk surgawi dalam agama India yang berhubungan dengan musik dan tari.
statement.en: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Indian religions associated with music and dance.

basis_claims.quote: In Hinduism, the gandharvas (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व, romanized: gandharva) are a class of minor deities who serve as divine musicians in Hindu mythology.

statement.id: Dalam Hindu mereka merupakan dewa kecil yang menjadi musisi ilahi.
statement.en: In Hinduism they are minor deities serving as divine musicians.

basis_claims.quote: Gandharvas usually live in Svarga and serve at Indra's court, though they also have their own realm, called the Gandharvaloka.

When they play on their divine instruments the fairy-like
Apsaras, who are all females, dance merrily.

basis_claims.quote: The Buckriders (Dutch: Bokkenrijders ; French: Chevaliers du bouc ) are a part of South-Eastern Dutch and North-Eastern Belgian folklore. They are witches, who rode through the sky on the back of flying bucks provided to them by the Devil to rob and murder common people and church possessions. ... Once a year, they would visit their master, the Devil, on the Mook Heath.

statement.id: Bokkenrijders (Prancis: Chevaliers du bouc) adalah bagian dari cerita rakyat Belanda tenggara dan Belgia timur laut: penyihir yang terbang menunggangi kambing jantan pemberian Iblis untuk merampok dan membunuh rakyat serta merampas harta gereja, dan setahun sekali mereka menghadap Iblis di Padang Mook.
statement.en: The Buckriders (Dutch Bokkenrijders, French Chevaliers du bouc) belong to south-eastern Dutch and north-eastern Belgian folklore: witches flying on bucks from the Devil to rob and murder people and church property, who once a year visited the Devil on the Mook Heath.

basis_claims.quote: The belief existed that the buckriders could travel fast and vast distances through the skies to rob in a widespread area and be home before dawn to remain obscured in their crimes.

statement.id: Ada kepercayaan bahwa bokkenrijders dapat menempuh jarak jauh dengan cepat lewat udara untuk merampok di wilayah luas dan pulang sebelum fajar agar kejahatannya tersembunyi.
statement.en: It was believed the buckriders could travel fast and far through the skies to rob over a wide area and be home before dawn, hiding their crimes.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed for rider; supernatural flying goat mount distinguishes this folklore.

fenixmannlein.aura: One small human-shaped Silesian earth sprite, intermediate in size between a dwarf and a human, in modest worn old rural clothing with ordinary rounded ears, taking a cabbage-like baked cake from a stone oven in a hill cave. The warmly lit cavern is cozy yet mysteriously hidden, smoke rises toward a small earth opening overhead. One figure, no invisible duplicate hand. Supernatural secret baker atmosphere; no flames shaped into phoenix wings or invented bird anatomy.

basis_claims.quote: are earth sprites and dwarves from German folklore. They were historically known in Silesia, particularly in the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník as well as in the part of Lusatia belonging to Saxony.

statement.id: Fenixmännlein (juga Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) adalah roh tanah dan kurcaci dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German), dahulu dikenal di Silesia, terutama Oderské vrchy dan Hrubý Jeseník, serta bagian Lusatia milik Sachsen (Saxony).
statement.en: The Fenixmännlein (also Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore, once known in Silesia, especially the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník, and in the Saxon part of Lusatia.

basis_claims.quote: The latter option is supported by the fact that both Fenixmännlein and Venedigermännlein are supposed to be bigger than dwarves (German Zwerge, sg. Zwerg) but smaller than humans. The Fenixmännlein are collective beings dwelling in hills and shrubbery.

statement.id: Asal nama dari Venedigermännlein ("lelaki kecil dari Venesia") didukung fakta bahwa keduanya lebih besar dari kurcaci tetapi lebih kecil dari manusia; Fenixmännlein hidup berkelompok di bukit dan semak.
statement.en: Derivation from the Venedigermännlein ('little Venetian men') is supported since both are bigger than dwarfs but smaller than humans; the Fenixmännlein live collectively in hills and shrubbery.

basis_claims.quote: Inside the mountains, they throw big parties. The Fenismannla (pl. Mannla = little men in Silesian German) are said to be the original owners of the recipe for Silesian streuselkuchen. When the Fänismännchen (sg., pl.;Männchen = little man) are baking cake in their caves, smoke is rising from earth holes and from beneath clods.

statement.id: Di dalam gunung mereka berpesta besar; mereka konon pemilik asli resep kue streusel Silesia (Silesian streuselkuchen), dan saat mereka memanggang di gua, asap naik dari lubang tanah.
statement.en: Inside the mountains they hold big parties; they are said to own the original Silesian streuselkuchen recipe, and when they bake in their caves smoke rises from earth holes.

basis_claims.quote: Immediately, an invisible hand gave him a Krautkuchen (cabbage cake) coated with green linseed oil. At the same time, he got threatened to eat this cake on a table made from iron or else he would be done for. The ploughboy fulfilled the condition by using his ploughshare as the iron table.

statement.id: Seorang pembajak yang meminta kue segera diberi kue kubis berlapis minyak biji rami oleh tangan tak terlihat, dengan ancaman harus memakannya di atas meja besi; ia memakai mata bajaknya sebagai meja besi.
statement.en: A ploughboy who asked for cake was at once handed a cabbage cake with linseed oil by an invisible hand, threatened to eat it on an iron table; he used his ploughshare as that table.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; earth sprite in mountain cave associated with hidden baking and cave smoke.

turst.aura: One dreadful but human-shaped Swiss spectral huntsman Türst, selecting Rickenbach GREEN hunting dress. Adult stern man in green coat and old hat sounding a curved hunting horn with one normal hand; other hand relaxed. Stormy Lucerne farm landscape in winter before Epiphany, open barn doorway behind and windblown clouds. No dogs pictured; distinctive three-legged or hybrid anatomy belongs to accompanying pack, not Türst, and MUST NOT be put on him. Ominous supernatural Wild Hunt atmosphere, normal ears and two human legs.

basis_claims.quote: is a legendary folkloric figure from the agricultural communities of Lucerne, dating to the pre-Christian era. He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. Türst blows his hunting horn through villages in the tempestuous months preceding Epiphany, accompanied by a baying pack of three-legged hunting dogs.

statement.id: Türst adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dari komunitas petani Luzern yang berasal dari masa pra-Kristen, digambarkan sebagai "pemburu mengerikan" yang harus diwaspadai saat cuaca berbadai; ia meniup terompet berburu menembus desa-desa pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani bersama kawanan anjing berkaki tiga.
statement.en: Türst is a folk figure of Lucerne's farming communities dating to pre-Christian times, a 'dreadful huntsman' to beware of in stormy weather, who blows his horn through villages in the stormy months before Epiphany with a pack of three-legged hounds.

basis_claims.quote: He appears in a green hunting costume in Rickenbach, accompanied by a pack of animals which are half dog and half pig. In Wolhusen, to avoid Türst, the citizens erected crosses. If a cross were to fall, the farmers would have bad luck until the cross stood straight again. The local people of Pilatus say that Türst is a ghost and a "dreadful huntsman"

statement.id: Di Rickenbach ia tampil berpakaian berburu hijau dengan kawanan setengah anjing setengah babi; di Wolhusen warga mendirikan salib untuk menghindarinya, dan bila salib roboh petani akan sial sampai salib ditegakkan; warga Pilatus menyebutnya hantu dan "pemburu mengerikan".
statement.en: In Rickenbach he appears in green hunting dress with a half-dog, half-pig pack; in Wolhusen people raised crosses against him, and a fallen cross brought farmers bad luck until set upright; the people of Pilatus call him a ghost and a 'dreadful huntsman'.

basis_claims.quote: Der Türst (auch Dürst genannt) ist eine Sagenfigur aus dem Luzerner Hinterland, die noch aus heidnischen Zeiten stammt. Er wird als „höllischer Jäger“ bezeichnet

statement.id: Türst (juga disebut Dürst) adalah tokoh legenda dari pedalaman Luzern yang berasal dari masa kafir dan disebut "pemburu neraka".
statement.en: Türst (also called Dürst) is a legendary figure from the Lucerne hinterland dating from heathen times, called the 'hellish huntsman'.

basis_claims.quote: It is also said that barn doors should stay open at this time, enabling Türst to hunt through the barn unhindered. Sträggele, his wife, appears in some Türst legends. Other legends say that Türst terrifies dairy cows, causing them to sicken and cease their milk production.

statement.id: Konon pintu lumbung harus dibiarkan terbuka pada masa itu agar Türst dapat berburu menembus lumbung tanpa halangan; istrinya Sträggele muncul dalam sebagian legenda, dan legenda lain menyebut ia menakuti sapi perah hingga sakit dan berhenti menghasilkan susu.
statement.en: Barn doors should be left open at this time so Türst can hunt through unhindered; his wife Sträggele appears in some legends, and others say he terrifies dairy cows until they sicken and stop giving milk.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; green-clad dreadful huntsman blowing horn in storm, a supernatural hunt leader.

basis_claims.quote: "he who drinks in might"), also found as Móðsognir ([ˈmoːðˌsoɣnez̠] ; Hauksbók manuscript variant), "he who drinks in courage", is the ruler of the dwarves. In Völuspà 10, he is identified as mæztr um orðinn dverga allra, "lord of all the dwarves".

statement.en: Mótsognir ('he who drinks in might'), also Móðsognir in the Hauksbók variant ('he who drinks in courage'), is ruler of the dwarfs; Völuspá 10 calls him 'lord of all the dwarves'.

basis_claims.quote: "the dwarfs had taken shape first and acquired life in the flesh of Ymir and were then maggots, but by decision of the gods they became conscious with intelligence and had the shape of men though they live in the earth and in rocks. Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn."

statement.id: Menurut Snorri dalam Gylfaginning 14, para kurcaci mula-mula terbentuk dan hidup di daging Ymir sebagai belatung, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh kesadaran, akal, dan rupa manusia walau tinggal di tanah dan bebatuan; Modsognir kurcaci pertama dan Durinn yang kedua.
statement.en: Per Snorri in Gylfaginning 14, the dwarfs first took shape and life in Ymir's flesh as maggots, then by the gods' decision gained awareness, intelligence and human shape though living in earth and rocks; Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn.

basis_claims.quote: According to Völuspà 9, the dwarfs were created by ginnheilög goð, "the high holy gods", who resolved to fashion them "out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones," a phrase typically interpreted to mean the blood and flesh of the primordial giant, Ymir.

statement.id: Menurut Völuspá 9, para kurcaci diciptakan "dewa-dewa yang mahasuci" yang memutuskan membentuk mereka "dari darah Brimir dan tulang Blainn", ungkapan yang biasa ditafsirkan sebagai darah dan daging raksasa purba Ymir.
statement.en: According to Völuspá 9, the dwarfs were made by 'the high holy gods', who resolved to shape them 'out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones', usually read as the blood and flesh of the primordial giant Ymir.

basis_claims.quote: Modsognir, auch Motsognir (altnordisch Módsognir bzw. Mótsognir), ist in der nordischen Mythologie der erste Zwerg und wurde von den Göttern erschaffen. Umstritten ist die Bedeutung des Namens, am ehesten könnte man ihn mit ‚der Müde, der Kraftlose‘ wiedergeben

statement.id: Modsognir atau Motsognir adalah kurcaci pertama dalam mitologi Nordik yang diciptakan para dewa; arti namanya diperdebatkan, paling mungkin "yang lelah, yang tak bertenaga".
statement.en: Modsognir or Motsognir is the first dwarf in Norse mythology, created by the gods; the meaning of the name is disputed, most likely 'the weary, powerless one'.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; principal dwarf in documented human-shaped post-origin stage.
motsognir.historical_basis: Mótsognir ('he who drinks in might'), also Móðsognir in the Hauksbók variant ('he who drinks in courage'), is ruler of the dwarfs; Völuspá 10 calls him 'lord of all the dwarves'. Per Snorri in Gylfaginning 14, the dwarfs first took shape and life in Ymir's flesh as maggots, then by the gods' decision gained awareness, intelligence and human shape though living in earth and rocks; Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn. According to Völuspá 9, the dwarfs were made by 'the high holy gods', who resolved to shape them 'out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones', usually read as the blood and flesh of the primordial giant Ymir. Modsognir or Motsognir is the first dwarf in Norse mythology, created by the gods; the meaning of the name is disputed, most likely 'the weary, powerless one'.

erlking.aura: One sinister human-shaped elderly forest elf-king from Goethe's literary Erlkönig, long beard and simple crown atop white hair, wearing a modest long archaic cloak, reaching one ordinary hand from among dark alder trunks. Full solitary figure contained within picture, no child or traveller visible. Silent deeply unsettling predatory woodland mood from night, mist and facial expression. Ordinary rounded human ears, no tree-bark body, antlers, wings or animal anatomy. A literary supernatural king portrait rather than a literal alder-tree hybrid.

basis_claims.quote: In European folklore and myth, the Erlking is a sinister elf who lingers in the woods. He stalks children who stay in the woods for too long and kills them with a single touch.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitos Eropa, Erlking adalah elf jahat yang berdiam di hutan, mengintai anak-anak yang terlalu lama di hutan, dan membunuh mereka dengan sekali sentuh.
statement.en: In European folklore and myth the Erlking is a sinister elf lingering in the woods, stalking children who stay too long and killing them with a single touch.

basis_claims.quote: is a name used in German Romanticism for the figure of a spirit or "king of the fairies". It is usually assumed that the name is a derivation from the ellekonge (older elverkonge, i.e. "Elf-king") in Danish folklore.

statement.id: Nama Erlking (Erlkönig, "raja pohon alder") dipakai dalam Romantisisme Jerman untuk roh atau "raja para peri" dan umumnya dianggap turunan dari ellekonge (lebih tua: elverkonge, "raja elf") dalam cerita rakyat Denmark.
statement.en: The name Erlking (Erlkönig, 'alder-king') was used in German Romanticism for a spirit or 'king of the fairies' and is usually thought to derive from Danish folklore's ellekonge (older elverkonge, 'elf-king').

basis_claims.quote: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in his ballad Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), an adaptation of the Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), and was taken up by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in his poem Erlkönig (1782), which was set to music by Schubert and others. Goethe added a new meaning, as "Erl" means not "elf" but "black alder"

statement.id: Nama ini pertama dipakai Johann Gottfried Herder dalam balada Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), saduran balada rakyat Denmark Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), lalu diambil Goethe dalam puisi Erlkönig (1782) yang digubah Schubert dan lainnya; Goethe menambah makna baru karena "Erl" berarti "alder hitam", bukan "elf".
statement.en: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), adapted from the Danish ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), then taken up by Goethe in Erlkönig (1782), set by Schubert and others; Goethe added a new sense, 'Erl' meaning 'black alder', not 'elf'.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; sinister supernatural king among alder trees.

The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), adapted from the Danish ballad Hr. clurichaun.aura: One six-inch-tall old male Irish cellar fairy Naggeneen, with a wrinkled human face LIKE a withered apple, wearing modest old little red-toned garments as illustration, perched beside a wine cask drinking from a tiny cup. Huge cask bung and ordinary wine-bottle silhouette establish miniature scale. Normal human anatomy and rounded ears, never a literal apple head. Uncanny mischievous wine-cellar mood, candlelight against damp deep stone.

basis_claims.quote: is a mischievous fairy in Irish folklore known for his great love of drinking and a tendency to haunt breweries, pubs and wine cellars. He is related to the leprechaun and has sometimes been conflated with him as a shoemaker and a guardian of hidden treasure. This has led some folklorists to suppose that the clurichaun is merely a leprechaun on a drinking spree

statement.id: Clurichaun (clúrachán, Irlandia/Irish clobhair-ceann) peri jahil cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), gemar minum, menghantui gudang anggur; kerabat leprechaun; di Irlandia.
statement.en: The clurichaun (clúrachán, Irish clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore who loves drink and haunts cellars; related to the leprechaun.

basis_claims.quote: Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy, encountered alone rather than in groups, as distinct from the trooping fairies.

statement.id: Seperti leprechaun, clurichaun peri penyendiri.
statement.en: Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy.

basis_claims.quote: In the folktale "The Haunted Cellar", recorded by Thomas Crofton Croker in 1825, a clurichaun named Naggeneen haunts the wine cellar of an Irish lord, drinking everything in sight and playing frightening pranks on the servants. He is described as a little man measuring 6 in (150 mm) tall, with a face like a withered apple.

statement.id: Dalam The Haunted Cellar (Croker, Thomas Crofton Croker, 1825), Naggeneen menghantui gudang anggur bangsawan Irlandia (Irish), setinggi 15 cm, wajah seperti apel layu; topi merah, gesper perak.
statement.en: In The Haunted Cellar (Thomas Crofton Croker, 1825), Naggeneen haunts an Irish lord's cellar, 6 in tall, face like a withered apple.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; six-inch supernatural wine-cellar haunter, withered-apple face simile retained as wrinkles.
clurichaun.historical_basis: The clurichaun (clúrachán, Irish clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore who loves drink and haunts cellars; related to the leprechaun. Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy. In The Haunted Cellar (Thomas Crofton Croker, 1825), Naggeneen haunts an Irish lord's cellar, 6 in tall, face like a withered apple.

onryo.aura: One human-shaped resentful spirit of Sugawara no Michizane in a restrained historically informed Heian Japanese court robe and black eboshi cap, stern scholarly adult male face, standing alone before distant palace roofs under a violent thunderstorm. Entire human body retained, two coherent human hands, normal face, no corpse deformation, horns, animal legs or modern horror woman costume. Ominous disaster-bearing spirit conveyed through storm and spectral moonlit atmosphere. No attack, victims or other deity. A spirit-stage portrait before later Tenjin worship; robe details illustrative.

basis_claims.quote: In ancient Japan, the spirits of the dead who died with resentment, called goryō 御霊 or onryō 怨霊, were thought to cast curses.

statement.id: Di Jepang kuno, onryō ialah arwah orang yang wafat dengan dendam dan dipercaya dapat mengutuk.
statement.en: In ancient Japan, onryō were spirits of the resentful dead believed to cast curses.

basis_claims.quote: Spirits thought to cause plague, natural disaster, or other such large-scale calamities were feared as onryō, and people tried to console and pacify them.

statement.id: Onryō ditakuti sebagai penyebab wabah dan bencana besar; orang berusaha menenangkan mereka.
statement.en: Onryō were feared as causes of plague and disasters and were pacified.

basis_claims.quote: Michizane was a distinguished scholar, poet, and statesman who died in exile, having been slandered by enemies at court.

statement.id: Michizane adalah cendekiawan dan pejabat yang meninggal dalam pengasingan.
statement.en: Michizane was a scholar and statesman who died in exile.

basis_claims.quote: After his death, a series of extraordinary natural disasters and plagues caused the untimely deaths of his detractors. In an attempt to appease his vengeful spirit, he was posthumously pardoned and promoted to high office, but the disasters continued.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, bencana dan wabah mengikuti kematiannya; ia diampuni dan dinaikkan pangkat untuk menenangkan rohnya, namun bencana berlanjut.
statement.en: In legend disasters and plagues followed his death; he was pardoned and promoted to appease his spirit, but calamities continued.

basis_claims.quote: dedicated to Sugawara Michizane (845–903). Michizane was a distinguished scholar

statement.id: Kisah ini berhubungan dengan Sugawara Michizane.
statement.en: The account concerns Sugawara Michizane.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; resentful dead court scholar associated with curses and disaster after exile.

ameonna.aura: One mature human-shaped Japanese rain woman based on Toriyama Sekien: rain-soaked long dark hair, plain wet modest kimono fully covering body, standing in heavy night rain and visibly licking the back of one raised ordinary human hand. Other normal hand relaxed, coherent five-finger anatomy. Old Japanese courtyard bamboo and dark foliage backdrop, supernatural rain atmosphere conveyed by downpour and somber stillness. Human face with visible tongue lightly touching hand, no extra mouth, horns, webbed limbs or child-snatching narrative.

basis_claims.quote: Ameonna (雨(あめ)女(おんな), "rain woman") is a Japanese yōkai thought to call forth rain, illustrated in Toriyama Sekien's Konjaku Hyakki Shūi as a woman standing in the rain and licking her hand.

statement.id: Ameonna berarti perempuan hujan dan Sekien menggambarkannya di tengah hujan.
statement.en: Ameonna means rain woman and Sekien depicts her in rain.

basis_claims.quote: You’ll find her first in Toriyama Sekien’s book, Konjaku Hyakki Shūi, supplement to the 100 demons from the present and past. In it is a black and white depiction of a rain-soaked woman, very creepily licking her hand.

statement.id: Gambar Sekien menunjukkan perempuan basah yang menjilat tangannya.
statement.en: Sekien pictures a rain-soaked woman licking her hand.

basis_claims.quote: It is said that the divine woman of Mount Wu in ancient China becomes a cloud in the morning and rain in the evening. I wonder if Ame-onna is also this kind of being.

statement.id: Keterangan Sekien membandingkan ameonna dengan perempuan ilahi Gunung Wu.
statement.en: Sekien compares ameonna with the divine woman of Mount Wu.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; supernatural rain woman performing documented hand-licking gesture.
ameonna.historical_basis: Ameonna means rain woman and Sekien depicts her in rain. Sekien pictures a rain-soaked woman licking her hand. Sekien compares ameonna with the divine woman of Mount Wu.
