basis_claims.quote: Poludnitsa (from: Polden or Poluden, 'half-day' or 'midday') is a mythical character common to the various Slavic countries of Eastern Europe.

statement.id: Poludnitsa (dari Polden atau Poluden, "setengah hari" atau "tengah hari") adalah tokoh mitos yang dikenal di berbagai negeri Slavia di Eropa Timur.
statement.en: Poludnitsa (from Polden or Poluden, "half-day" or "midday") is a mythical character common to various Slavic countries of Eastern Europe.

basis_claims.quote: Poludnitsa is a noon demon in Slavic mythology. She can be referred to in English as "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith" or "noon witch".

statement.id: Poludnitsa adalah iblis siang hari dalam mitologi Slavia; dalam bahasa Inggris ia disebut "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith", atau "noon witch".
statement.en: Poludnitsa is a noon demon in Slavic mythology, called in English "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith" or "noon witch".

basis_claims.quote: She was usually pictured as a young woman dressed in white that roamed field bounds. She assailed folk working at noon, causing heatstrokes and aches in the neck; sometimes she even caused madness.

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda berbaju putih yang berkeliaran di pematang ladang; ia menyerang orang yang bekerja pada tengah hari, menyebabkan sengatan panas dan sakit leher, kadang bahkan kegilaan.
statement.en: She was usually pictured as a young woman in white roaming field bounds; she attacked people working at noon, causing heatstroke and neck pain, sometimes even madness.

basis_claims.quote: Poludnitsa, who makes herself evident in the middle of hot summer days, takes the form of whirling dust clouds and carries a scythe, sickle or shears

statement.id: Poludnitsa muncul di tengah hari musim panas yang terik dalam bentuk pusaran debu dan membawa sabit, arit, atau gunting.
statement.en: Poludnitsa appears in the middle of hot summer days as whirling dust clouds and carries a scythe, sickle or shears.

basis_claims.quote: She may appear as an old hag, a beautiful woman, or a 12-year-old girl, and she was useful in scaring children away from valuable crops. She is only seen on the hottest part of the day and is a personification of a sun-stroke.

statement.id: Ia bisa tampil sebagai nenek tua, perempuan cantik, atau gadis berusia 12 tahun, dan berguna untuk menakuti anak agar menjauhi tanaman berharga; ia hanya terlihat pada saat paling panas dan merupakan personifikasi sengatan matahari.
statement.en: She may appear as an old hag, a beautiful woman or a 12-year-old girl, and served to scare children from valuable crops; she is seen only in the hottest part of the day and personifies sunstroke.

basis_claims.quote: Согласно большинству представлений, полудница — враждебна и очень опасна для людей.

statement.id: Menurut kebanyakan kepercayaan, poludnitsa bermusuhan dan sangat berbahaya bagi manusia.
statement.en: According to most beliefs, the poludnitsa is hostile and very dangerous to people.

basis_claims.quote: is an ugly and mischievous or mad old woman living in the forest (in the heart of virgin forests, in a hut/cabin, or an old tree). She is the opposite of fairies such as Zână. She is also the protector of the animals and plants, brewing potions and helping injured animals.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, Muma Pădurii adalah perempuan tua buruk rupa yang nakal atau gila, tinggal di hutan (jantung hutan perawan, pondok, atau pohon tua), lawan peri seperti Zână, sekaligus pelindung hewan dan tumbuhan yang meracik ramuan dan menolong hewan terluka.
statement.en: In Romanian folklore Muma Pădurii is an ugly, mischievous or mad old woman living in the forest (deep virgin forest, a hut or an old tree), the opposite of fairies such as the Zână, and protector of animals and plants who brews potions and helps injured animals.

basis_claims.quote: She cures the forest if it is dying and she keeps unwanted trespassers away by driving them mad and scaring them.

statement.id: Ia menyembuhkan hutan yang sekarat dan mengusir penyusup dengan membuat mereka gila dan ketakutan; ia makhluk netral yang hanya mencelakai orang yang merusak hutan.
statement.en: She cures a dying forest and keeps trespassers away by driving them mad and scaring them.

basis_claims.quote: Mumă Pădurii es un espíritu del bosque en el cuerpo de una mujer muy fea y anciana. A veces tiene la habilidad de cambiar de forma. Suele vivir en una casita oscura, terrible y escondida.

statement.id: Muma Pădurii adalah roh hutan dalam tubuh perempuan yang sangat buruk rupa dan tua; kadang ia dapat berubah wujud, dan biasanya tinggal di rumah kecil yang gelap, mengerikan, dan tersembunyi.
statement.en: Muma Pădurii is a forest spirit in the body of a very ugly old woman; she can sometimes change shape and usually lives in a dark, dreadful, hidden little house.

basis_claims.quote: Muma Pădurii (em tradução livre "Mãe da Floresta" em romeno, também conhecida como Pădureanca ou Muma Huciului)

basis_claims.quote: Según las creencias populares canarias, las llamadas brujas del Bailadero de Anaga eran mujeres que se dedicaban a hacer aquelarres en una zona montañosa del noreste de la isla de Tenerife

basis_claims.quote: In Albanian mythology, the shtojzovalle, also known as shtojzorreshta, shtozote is a small creature with supernatural powers and of extraordinary beauty. They are invisible woodland creatures, which can be seen by humans only on rare occasions and are fond of song and dance.

statement.en: In Albanian mythology the shtojzovalle (also shtojzorreshta or shtozote) is a small creature with supernatural powers and extraordinary beauty; they are invisible woodland creatures, rarely seen by humans, fond of song and dance.

basis_claims.quote: They live in forests and pastures and spend their time singing and dancing. They have the ability to fly and at night they spin the thread of human existence. They are invisible to humans and a human can see them only if they lift an invisible veil in front of their eyes.

statement.en: They live in forests and pastures, spend their time singing and dancing, can fly, and at night spin the thread of human existence; a human can see them only by lifting an invisible veil before their eyes.

basis_claims.quote: Occasionally humans and shtojzovalles are married, but a human can keep a shtojzovalle maiden only if he gives her his clothes to wear.

statement.id: Kadang manusia dan shtojzovalle menikah, tetapi seorang lelaki hanya dapat mempertahankan gadis shtojzovalle jika ia memberikan pakaiannya untuk dikenakan sang gadis.

basis_claims.quote: According to this legend, the Hinzelmann ("Hintzelmann" in the original source) began haunting the castle Hudemühlen in Lower Saxony beginning in the year 1584. statement.id: Menurut legenda, Hinzelmann (dalam sumber asli Hintzelmann) mulai menghantui Kastel Hudemühlen di Niedersachsen pada 1584; mula-mula hanya terdengar gedoran, lalu ia mengaku bernama Lüring, beristri Hille Bingels, dan dulu tinggal di pegunungan Hutan Bohemia.
statement.en: By the legend Hinzelmann ('Hintzelmann' in the source) began haunting Hudemühlen Castle in Lower Saxony in 1584; at first only banging was heard, then he said he was named Lüring, had a wife Hille Bingels and once lived in the Bohemian Forest mountains.

statement.en: Hinzelmann dutifully did kitchen chores such as washing dishes and scrubbing cookware, recovered lost items and groomed horses; he gave advice but could strike with a stick if ignored, and the cook or servants had to set out a bowl of sweet milk with crumbled white bread.

basis_claims.quote: Hinzelmann (auch Lüring) ist die Bezeichnung für einen Kobold als Sagengestalt. Er soll Gutes, wie die Erledigung von Hausarbeit, vollbracht haben. Er konnte aber auch böse werden, wenn man ihn reizte. Dabei trat Hinzelmann ohne Gestalt auf und hatte die Stimme eines Kindes. ... 1588 ging er freiwillig von Hudemühlen fort und ließ sich danach in Eystrup nieder.

statement.id: Hinzelmann (juga Lüring) adalah kobold dalam sage yang konon berbuat baik seperti mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah, tetapi bisa jahat bila diganggu; ia tampil tanpa wujud dengan suara anak kecil, dan pada 1588 pergi dengan sukarela dari Hudemühlen lalu menetap di Eystrup.
statement.en: Hinzelmann (also Lüring) is a legendary kobold said to have done good, such as housework, but could turn nasty if provoked; he appeared without form and with a child's voice, and in 1588 left Hudemühlen of his own accord and settled in Eystrup.

statement.en: On the other hand, when treated well, he does the housework at night.

basis_claims.quote: Rather, they were buried outside the territory of a church, in places such as at crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps, or ravines, since it was believed that they were "cursed by their parents and the earth would not receive them."

statement.en: They were buried outside church grounds, at places such as crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps or ravines, because they were believed to be "cursed by their parents, and the earth would not receive them".

basis_claims.quote: In Finnish folklore, all places and things, and also human beings, have a haltija (a genie, guardian spirit) of their own.  One such haltija is called etiäinen—an image, doppelgänger, or just an impression that goes ahead of a person, doing things the person in question later does.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, semua tempat, benda, dan manusia punya haltija (roh penjaga); salah satunya etiäinen, bayangan, kembaran, atau kesan yang mendahului seseorang dan melakukan hal yang kelak ia lakukan.
statement.en: In Finnish folklore all places, things and people have a haltija (guardian spirit); one is the etiäinen, an image, doppelgänger or impression that goes ahead of a person doing what they later do.

basis_claims.quote: Etiäinen can also refer to some kind of a feeling that something is going to happen. Sometimes it could, for example, warn of a bad year coming.

statement.id: Etiäinen juga bisa berarti perasaan bahwa sesuatu akan terjadi, misalnya peringatan akan datangnya tahun yang buruk.
statement.en: Etiäinen can also mean a feeling that something is going to happen, for example a warning of a bad year coming.

basis_claims.quote: In modern Finnish, the term has detached from its shamanistic origins and refers to premonition. Unlike clairvoyance, divination, and similar practices, etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous and cannot be induced. Quite the opposite, they may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Finlandia modern istilah ini lepas dari asal syamanistiknya dan berarti firasat; etiäiset (jamak) bersifat spontan, tidak bisa dipanggil, dan dapat tidak diinginkan serta menimbulkan kecemasan seperti hantu.
statement.en: In modern Finnish the term has left its shamanistic origins and means premonition; etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous, cannot be induced, and may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.

basis_claims.quote: Ihmiset saattavat kuulla esimerkiksi perheenjäsenensä kävelevän pihaan, avaavan oven, jopa nähdä tämän hahmon tai varjon, kunnes huomaavat, ettei tämä todellisuudessa vielä tullutkaan. Pian perheenjäsen kuitenkin tulee ja toistaa saman kuin etiäisensä.

statement.id: Orang bisa mendengar anggota keluarganya masuk halaman dan membuka pintu, bahkan melihat sosok atau bayangannya, lalu sadar ia belum datang; tak lama ia benar-benar datang dan mengulangi apa yang dilakukan etiäinen-nya.

basis_claims.quote: Les Lavandières, or the Midnight Washerwomen, are three old washerwomen in Celtic mythology. Names in various Celtic languages include the kannerezed noz in Brittany and the Bean nighe in Gaelic. They can also be found in the Celtic folklore of Iberia as Las Lavanderas in Cantabria, As lavandeiras in Galicia or Les Llavanderes in Asturias, and in Portugal are known as Bruxas lavadeiras .

statement.id: Les Lavandières (Midnight Washerwomen) tiga pencuci tua mitologi Kelt (Celtic mythology); kannerezed noz di Brittany, Bean nighe (Gaelic, Gaelik); Iberia: Las Lavanderas (Cantabria), As lavandeiras (Galicia), Les Llavanderes (Asturias), Bruxas lavadeiras (Portugal); di Spanyol dan Portugal.
statement.en: Les Lavandières (Midnight Washerwomen) are three old Celtic washerwomen; kannerezed noz in Brittany, Bean nighe in Gaelic; in Iberia Las Lavanderas, As lavandeiras, Les Llavanderes, Bruxas lavadeiras.

basis_claims.quote: The three old women go to the water's edge at midnight to wash shrouds for those about to die, according to the myth and folklore of Brittany; or to wash the bloodstained clothing of those who are about to die, according to Celtic mythology. The Midnight Washerwomen may be related to the old Celtic tradition of the triple goddess of death and slaughter.

statement.id: Tengah malam mencuci kain kafan orang yang akan mati (Brittany) atau pakaian berdarah (Celtic); terkait dewi tiga kematian.
statement.en: At midnight they wash shrouds for the soon-to-die (Brittany) or bloodstained clothes (Celtic myth); linked to the triple goddess of death.

basis_claims.quote: The washerwomen are small, dressed in green and have webbed feet. Their webbed feet may be the reason they are also sometimes called the cannard noz (meaning "night ducks") in Breton folklore.

statement.id: Kecil, berpakaian hijau, berkaki berselaput; cannard noz, bebek malam (Breton folklore).
statement.en: Small, green-clad, web-footed; cannard noz, night ducks (Breton folklore).

basis_claims.quote: The Breton washerwomen wash graveclothes, usually at night, under the moonlight, and are notable for their intense dislike of being disturbed, cursing those who dare to do so. They are known to ask passers-by for help in wringing clothes, breaking the arms of those who do so reluctantly and drowning those who refuse.

statement.id: Pencuci Breton mencuci kain kubur malam hari, benci diganggu; mematahkan lengan dan menenggelamkan.
statement.en: Breton washerwomen wash graveclothes at night, hate disturbance, break arms and drown.

basis_claims.quote: Maa-alused are, in Estonian folk religion, mysterious elf-like creatures which live beneath the ground.

statement.id: Dalam agama rakyat Estonia, maa-alused adalah makhluk misterius mirip peri yang hidup di bawah tanah.
statement.en: In Estonian folk religion, maa-alused are mysterious elf-like creatures that live beneath the ground.

basis_claims.quote: They were believed to have a parallel existence to that of humans, the principal differences being that all orientations are reversed, such that up becomes down and left becomes right, and that all things possessed by them are diminished in size.

statement.id: Mereka dipercaya hidup sejajar dengan manusia, dengan perbedaan utama bahwa semua arah terbalik, atas menjadi bawah dan kiri menjadi kanan, dan semua milik mereka berukuran lebih kecil.
statement.en: They were believed to live a parallel existence to humans, the main differences being that all orientations are reversed, up becoming down and left becoming right, and that everything they own is smaller in size.

basis_claims.quote: Maa-alused (ka maahaldjad) olid algselt surnud olendid, kes hiljem elasid maa või põranda all.

statement.id: Maa-alused (juga disebut maahaldjad) semula adalah makhluk yang sudah mati, yang kemudian hidup di bawah tanah atau di bawah lantai.
statement.en: Maa-alused (also maahaldjad) were originally dead beings who later lived under the ground or under the floor.

basis_claims.quote: Maa-alused olid tuntud pisikeste inimesekujuliste mütoloogiliste olenditena põhiliselt Põhja-Eestis, nende olemasolust andsid märku hääled. Nad tegutsesid seppade (taovad tiks-tiks) ja kangrutena, maa peale ilmusid ka putuka või loomana (harilikult konnana). Neile tehtud heategude eest tasusid rikkalikult.

statement.id: Maa-alused dikenal sebagai makhluk mitos kecil berwujud manusia, terutama di Estonia Utara (Põhja-Eesti), yang keberadaannya ditandai suara-suara; mereka bekerja sebagai pandai besi (berbunyi tiks-tiks) dan penenun, muncul di atas tanah sebagai serangga atau hewan (biasanya katak), dan membalas kebaikan dengan murah hati.
statement.en: Maa-alused were known as tiny human-shaped mythical beings mainly in North Estonia (Põhja-Eesti), whose presence was signalled by sounds; they worked as smiths (hammering tiks-tiks) and weavers, appeared above ground as insects or animals (usually frogs), and repaid good deeds generously.

basis_claims.quote: Vâlvă (plural vâlve) is a female spirit mentioned in the Romanian folklore. statement.id: Vâlvă (jamak vâlve) adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya berjalan di puncak-puncak bukit pada malam hari; mereka terbagi menjadi Vâlve Albe ("Vâlve Putih") yang baik dan Vâlve Negre ("Vâlve Hitam") yang jahat.

basis_claims.quote: They may also appear under various guises, such as shadows or black cats. They also have the ability to shapeshift.

basis_claims.quote: Вылвы могут принимать разный облик. Часто они выглядят как женщины, иногда просто как тени или чёрные кошки. Вылвы могут защищать село от бури, града, урагана.

statement.id: Vâlve bisa mengambil berbagai wujud: sering seperti perempuan, kadang hanya bayangan atau kucing hitam; mereka bisa melindungi desa dari badai, hujan es, dan angin topan.
statement.en: Vâlve can take various forms: often women, sometimes mere shadows or black cats; they can protect a village from storm, hail and hurricane.

basis_claims.quote: is a night spirit (Bogeyman) in Slavic folklore. According to beliefs, he abducts children who do not sleep at night or behave badly. He is also called Babayka (Russian: Бабайка), Babayko (Ukrainian: Бабайко) or Bobo (Babok, Bebok) (Polish)

statement.id: Babay (Бабай) adalah roh malam (momok) dalam cerita rakyat Slavia yang menculik anak yang tidak tidur atau nakal; juga disebut Babayka, Babayko (Ukraina), atau Bobo (Polandia).
statement.en: Babay is a night spirit (bogeyman) of Slavic folklore who abducts children who do not sleep or behave badly; also called Babayka, Babayko (Ukrainian) or Bobo (Polish).

basis_claims.quote: Babay is rarely described, so that children can imagine him in the form most terrible for them, but sometimes Babay is described as a pitch-black and crooked old man. He has some physical defects, such as muteness, armlessness, and/or lameness. He has a bag and a cane.

statement.id: Babay jarang digambarkan agar anak membayangkannya dalam wujud paling menakutkan, tetapi kadang ia lelaki tua hitam bengkok dengan cacat seperti bisu, tak berlengan, atau pincang, membawa karung dan tongkat; ia tinggal di hutan, rawa, atau kebun.
statement.en: Babay is rarely described so children imagine their worst form, but sometimes he is a pitch-black crooked old man with defects like muteness, armlessness or lameness, carrying a bag and cane; he lives in the forest, a swamp or a garden.

basis_claims.quote: King Alfons II of Aragon sent the old noble Count Arnald Estruc to fight paganism and witchcraft at Llers Castle (Alt Emporda) where the Count was killed in 1173. ... Count Estruch sucked blood from the villagers in the area and seduced and impregnated young women. After nine months, these women would give birth to monstrous newborns who were dead at birth.

statement.id: Raja Alfons II dari Aragon mengirim bangsawan tua Arnald Estruc ke Kastel Llers (Alt Empordà) untuk memerangi paganisme dan sihir, dan ia terbunuh di sana pada 1173; setelah itu ia mengisap darah penduduk dan menghamili perempuan muda, yang setelah sembilan bulan melahirkan bayi mengerikan yang mati saat lahir.
statement.en: King Alfons II of Aragon sent the old noble Arnald Estruc to Llers Castle (Alt Empordà) to fight paganism and witchcraft, where he was killed in 1173; afterwards he sucked villagers' blood and impregnated young women, who after nine months bore monstrous newborns dead at birth.

basis_claims.quote: Malgrat que l'autor afirma que la seva obra es basa en una llegenda que ell mateix recuperà d'una història del segle xii, mai no n'ha establert la fidelitat ni n'ha aportat cap prova. ... fa que, en general, els historiadors neguin la veracitat de la suposada llegenda i sostinguin que no hi ha rastres històrics de la figura d'Estruch.

statement.id: Para sejarawan umumnya menolak kebenaran legenda yang diklaim itu dan berpendapat tidak ada jejak sejarah sosok Estruch; penulisnya tidak pernah membuktikan sumber abad ke-12 yang ia klaim.
statement.en: Historians generally deny the truth of the supposed legend and hold that there is no historical trace of Estruch; the author never proved the 12th-century source he claimed.

basis_claims.quote: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being that is described in occult and alchemical works from around the time of the European Renaissance, and particularly elaborated in the 16th century works of Paracelsus.

statement.id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib mitis yang digambarkan dalam karya okultisme dan alkimia sekitar masa Renaisans Eropa, terutama dikembangkan dalam karya Paracelsus abad ke-16.
statement.en: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being described in occult and alchemical works from around the European Renaissance, especially developed in Paracelsus's 16th-century writings.

basis_claims.quote: According to Paracelsus and his subsequent followers, there are four categories of elementals, which are gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders. These correspond to the four Empedoclean elements of antiquity: earth, water, air, and fire, respectively.

statement.id: Menurut Paracelsus dan pengikutnya, ada empat jenis elemental, yaitu gnome, undine, sylph, dan salamander, yang sesuai dengan empat unsur Empedokles: tanah, air, udara, dan api.
statement.en: According to Paracelsus and his followers there are four kinds of elementals, gnomes, undines, sylphs and salamanders, matching the four Empedoclean elements: earth, water, air and fire.

basis_claims.quote: He regarded them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, generally being invisible to mankind but having physical and commonly humanoid bodies, as well as eating, sleeping, and wearing clothes like humans.

basis_claims.quote: (the "Beauty of the Earth" or "Earthly Beauty") is an epithet in Albanian mythology and folklore, used in some traditions for a crafty fairy, and in other traditions for a chthonic/earth goddess, the counterpart of e Bukura e Detit (the Beauty of the Sea) and i Bukuri i Qiellit (the Beauty of the Sky).

statement.id: E Bukura e Dheut ("Kecantikan Bumi") adalah julukan dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania bagi peri licik dalam sebagian tradisi dan dewi bumi atau dunia bawah dalam tradisi lain, pasangan e Bukura e Detit (Kecantikan Laut) dan i Bukuri i Qiellit (Kecantikan Langit).
statement.en: E Bukura e Dheut ("Beauty of the Earth") is an epithet in Albanian myth and folklore for a crafty fairy in some traditions and a chthonic or earth goddess in others, counterpart of e Bukura e Detit (Beauty of the Sea) and i Bukuri i Qiellit (Beauty of the Sky).

basis_claims.quote: E Bukura e Dheut is beauty made manifest, radiating with golden hair. statement.id: Ia kecantikan yang menjelma, bercahaya dengan rambut emas; bisa roh baik atau (lebih sering) jahat, kekuatan sihirnya dari pakaiannya, dan tinggal di dunia bawah dalam istana yang dijaga anjing berkepala tiga, kuçedra, dan makhluk aneh lainnya.
statement.en: She is beauty made manifest with golden hair; a good or (more often) evil spirit whose magic comes from her dress, living in the underworld in a palace guarded by a three-headed dog, a kuçedra and other strange creatures.

basis_claims.quote: The quest for the e Bukura e Dheut is a very popular and frequent motif in Albanian folktales: the princely hero must search for or rescue the Earthly Beauty, even going into her mystical underworld palace.

statement.id: Pencarian e Bukura e Dheut adalah motif sangat populer dalam dongeng Albania: pahlawan pangeran harus mencari atau menyelamatkannya, bahkan masuk ke istana mistisnya di dunia bawah.
statement.en: The quest for e Bukura e Dheut is a very popular motif in Albanian folktales: the princely hero must find or rescue her, even entering her mystical underworld palace.

basis_claims.quote: is a vampire in Polish folklore. According to legend, some people are born with the destiny of becoming vjesci, discernible by a caul located on the newborn's head. In order to prevent these individuals from becoming vjesci, the caul was removed, dried, ground and fed to the person on their seventh birthday.

statement.id: Vjesci adalah vampir dalam cerita rakyat Polandia; sebagian orang lahir ditakdirkan menjadi vjesci, tampak dari selaput ketuban di kepala bayi; untuk mencegahnya selaput itu dilepas, dikeringkan, digiling, dan diberikan pada ulang tahun ketujuh.
statement.en: The vjesci is a vampire of Polish folklore; some are born destined for it, marked by a caul on the head; to prevent it the caul was removed, dried, ground and fed to them on their seventh birthday.

basis_claims.quote: Typically, vjesci were said to be indistinguishable from humans, although in some stories, they had a ruddy complexion and an excitable nature. At the time of their death, a vjesci would refuse to take the sacrament. Their body would cool quickly, and their limbs would remain limber. Their lips and cheeks would remain red

statement.id: Vjesci biasanya tak bisa dibedakan dari manusia; saat mati ia menolak sakramen, tubuhnya cepat dingin, anggota badan tetap lentur, dan bibir serta pipinya tetap merah.
statement.en: Vjesci were usually indistinguishable from humans; at death they refused the sacrament, the body cooled quickly, the limbs stayed limber and lips and cheeks stayed red.

basis_claims.quote: the vjesci did not die, instead returning to life at midnight after its burial and eating its clothes and some of its own flesh. The vampire would leave the grave and return home to eat its family and neighbors. After visiting its relatives, it would go to the local church and ring the church bell. Those who heard the bell were supposedly destined to be the vampire's next victims.

statement.id: Vjesci tidak mati, melainkan bangkit pada tengah malam setelah dikubur, memakan pakaian dan sebagian dagingnya, meninggalkan kubur untuk memangsa keluarga dan tetangga, lalu membunyikan lonceng gereja; yang mendengarnya menjadi korban berikutnya.
statement.en: The vjesci did not die but rose at midnight after burial, ate its clothes and some of its flesh, left the grave to eat family and neighbours, then rang the church bell; those who heard it were its next victims.

basis_claims.quote: postać z zakresu demonologii słowiańskiej, będąca formą pośmiertnej egzystencji ludzkiej duszy, zbliżona do wyobrażeń upiora lub wampira, posiadająca jednak na wielu terenach własną, odrębną tożsamość

basis_claims.quote: Дворец Морского царя, сделанный из хрусталя, серебра, золота и драгоценных камней, помещается неопределённо: то в синем море, то на острове, то в Ильмень-озере. Когда он пляшет и развлекается — на море шторм и поднимается буря.

statement.id: Uriaș adalah tokoh mitologi atau dongeng berwajah manusia, besar, kekar, dan perkasa, setinggi beberapa depa, dengan langkah sejauh satu pos perjalanan dan kepala sebesar takaran gandum; mereka bisa mengobrol dari satu gunung ke gunung lain dan mampu berpegangan pada pegangan langit.
statement.en: The uriași are figures of myth or fairy tale with human faces, huge, brawny and strong, several fathoms tall, with a stride as long as a post-stage and heads as big as a grain measure; they can chat from one mountain to another and can grab the handles of the sky.

basis_claims.quote: Uneori sunt descriși ca ciclopi, cu un singur ochi în frunte și hrănindu-se cu carne de om.

statement.id: Kadang mereka digambarkan sebagai kiklops bermata satu di dahi yang memakan daging manusia.
statement.en: Sometimes they are described as cyclopes with a single eye in the forehead, feeding on human flesh.

basis_claims.quote: is a positive creature from Belarusian mythology said to live in fields. The name literally means "rye creature", from Belarusian жыта, "rye".

statement.id: Zhytsen atau Žycień adalah makhluk baik dalam mitologi Belarus yang konon tinggal di ladang; namanya secara harfiah berarti "makhluk gandum hitam", dari kata Belarus zhyta, "gandum hitam".
statement.en: Zhytsen or Žycień is a benevolent creature of Belarusian mythology said to live in fields; the name literally means "rye creature", from Belarusian zhyta, "rye".

basis_claims.quote: Zhyten is often called a spirit of wealth and wellbeing. It is believed that Zhytsen contributes to good ripening of crops and vegetables, and accordingly, Zhyten is considered the caretaker of good harvests.

statement.id: Zhytsen sering disebut roh kekayaan dan kesejahteraan; ia dipercaya membantu tanaman dan sayuran matang dengan baik, sehingga dianggap pengurus panen yang baik.
statement.en: Zhytsen is often called a spirit of wealth and wellbeing; it is believed to help crops and vegetables ripen well and so is considered the caretaker of good harvests.

basis_claims.quote: Zhytsen walks through the fields and ensures that crops there are well reaped. It is believed in Belarusian folklore that if Zhytsen finds some left ears of grain, it binds them in sheaves and brings to the fields of more diligent farmers.

statement.id: Zhytsen berjalan melintasi ladang memastikan panen dituai dengan baik; dalam folklor Belarus dipercaya bila ia menemukan bulir yang tertinggal, ia mengikatnya menjadi berkas dan membawanya ke ladang petani yang lebih rajin.
statement.en: Zhytsen walks the fields making sure the crops are well reaped; Belarusian folklore holds that if it finds ears of grain left behind, it binds them into sheaves and carries them to the fields of more diligent farmers.

basis_claims.quote: Как древнебелорусский бог плодородия и осени описан (и, вероятно, придуман) фольклористом Павлом Шпилевским (Древлянским).

statement.id: Sebagai dewa kesuburan dan musim gugur Belarus kuno, Zhytsen digambarkan, dan kemungkinan dikarang, oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).
statement.en: As an ancient Belarusian god of fertility and autumn, Zhytsen was described, and probably invented, by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).

basis_claims.quote: Особенностью Житеня является третий глаз на затылке, который нужен для лучшего выполнения задач этого мифологического персонажа.

statement.id: Ciri khas Zhytsen adalah mata ketiga di tengkuk, yang membantunya menjalankan tugasnya dengan lebih baik.
statement.en: A peculiarity of Zhytsen is a third eye on the back of the head, which helps it do its work better.

basis_claims.quote: На Беларусі Жыценя уяўлялі маленькім дзедам («Жытні дзед») з доўгай барадой.

statement.id: Di Belarus, Zhytsen dibayangkan sebagai kakek kecil ("Kakek Gandum Hitam") berjanggut panjang.
statement.en: In Belarus Zhytsen was imagined as a little old man ("Rye Grandfather") with a long beard.

basis_claims.quote: boginki (singular: boginka) are female spirits or demons of wild nature: forest, field, mountains, or water (both of land and sea) and is often a personification of the forces of nature. The word literally means "minor goddess" in Polish and may be translated as "fairy" or "nymph". They were usually imagined as either ugly old hags or pretty young girls, usually naked. They are usually evil.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, boginki (tunggal boginka) adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar (hutan, ladang, gunung, perairan), sering perwujudan kekuatan alam; kata ini berarti "dewi kecil" dan dapat diterjemahkan peri atau nimfa; mereka dibayangkan sebagai nenek buruk rupa atau gadis cantik, biasanya telanjang, dan umumnya jahat.
statement.en: In Polish pagan mythology boginki (singular boginka) are female spirits or demons of wild nature (forest, field, mountains, water), often personifying natural forces; the word means "minor goddess" and may be translated "fairy" or "nymph"; imagined as ugly hags or pretty girls, usually naked, and usually evil.

basis_claims.quote: В поверьях Оравы, Спиша и особенно Замагурья богинка описывается как злое уродливое существо c высокой нескладной фигурой, непропорционально большой головой, вздутым животом, кривыми ногами, чёрными зубами, большими грудями, которые закидывались назад через плечо. Также богинки могут появляться в виде животных — кошек, собак, лягушек и др.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan di Orava dan Spiš, boginka adalah makhluk jahat buruk rupa bertubuh tinggi canggung, berkepala besar, berperut buncit, berkaki bengkok, bergigi hitam, dan berpayudara besar yang disampirkan ke belakang bahu; boginki juga dapat muncul sebagai kucing, anjing, atau katak.
statement.en: In Orava and Spiš belief the boginka is an evil, ugly being, tall and gawky, with an oversized head, swollen belly, crooked legs, black teeth and large breasts thrown back over the shoulder; boginki can also appear as cats, dogs or frogs.

basis_claims.quote: Boginki zamieszkiwały bagna, jeziora, rzeki, lasy i góry. Można je było spotkać nad wodą podczas prania chust drewnianymi kijankami. ... Boginkami miały stawać się kobiety zmarłe przy porodzie, samobójczynie i morderczynie dzieci.

statement.id: Perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan, bunuh diri, atau membunuh anaknya dipercaya menjadi boginka; boginki tinggal di rawa, danau, sungai, hutan, dan gunung, dan dijumpai di tepi air saat mencuci kain.
statement.en: Women who died in childbirth, suicides and child-murderers were said to become boginki; they lived in marshes, lakes, rivers, forests and mountains and were met by the water washing cloths.

basis_claims.quote: is a ghostly spirit in Welsh mythology, a disembodied moaning voice that sounds before a person's death. Legends associate the cyhyraeth with the area around the River Tywi in eastern Dyfed, as well as the coast of Glamorganshire.

statement.id: Roh hantu mitologi Welsh (Wales), suara rintihan sebelum kematian; dikaitkan dengan Sungai Tywi (River Tywi), Dyfed timur, dan pesisir Glamorganshire.
statement.en: A ghostly spirit of Welsh mythology (Wales), a moaning voice before death; linked to the River Tywi, eastern Dyfed and the Glamorganshire coast.

basis_claims.quote: to sound three times (growing weaker and fainter each time) as a threefold warning before the person expires. Along the Glamorganshire coast, the cyhyraeth is said to be heard before a shipwreck, accompanied by a corpse-light.

statement.id: Terdengar tiga kali sebagai peringatan; di pesisir Glamorganshire sebelum kapal karam, dengan cahaya mayat (corpse-light).
statement.en: Sounds three times as a warning; on the Glamorganshire coast before a shipwreck, with a corpse-light.

basis_claims.quote: sind Geister der walisischen Mythologie mit einer körperlosen Stimme, die vor dem Tod eines Menschen zu hören sind.

statement.id: Roh mitologi Welsh dengan suara tanpa tubuh sebelum kematian.
statement.en: Spirits of Welsh mythology with a bodiless voice heard before a death.

basis_claims.quote: Wie die schottischen Cailleach und die irischen Banshee klagen Gwrach und Cyhyraeth auch über den Tod von Landsleuten in der Fremde.

statement.id: Seperti Cailleach dan Banshee, Gwrach dan Cyhyraeth meratapi orang sebangsa yang mati di negeri asing.
statement.en: Like the Cailleach and Banshee, Gwrach and Cyhyraeth lament countrymen dying abroad.

basis_claims.quote: is the god of death and the underworld, sometimes referred to as Tamag (hell) in Turkic mythology.

statement.id: Erlik adalah dewa kematian dan dunia bawah dalam mitologi Turkik, yang kadang disebut Tamag (neraka).
statement.en: Erlik is the god of death and the underworld in Turkic mythology, the underworld sometimes called Tamag (hell).

basis_claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, Erlik was involved in the creation of humanity. He slew the messenger-god, Maidere/Maydere, and is a teacher of sin. He is sometimes represented by a totemic bear.

statement.id: Erlik terlibat dalam penciptaan manusia, membunuh dewa utusan Maidere, dan mengajarkan dosa; kadang ia dilambangkan dengan beruang totem.
statement.en: Erlik took part in the creation of humanity, slew the messenger god Maidere and teaches sin; he is sometimes represented by a totemic bear.

basis_claims.quote: Erlik gilt als Ursache von Krankheit und Tod, und als Richter über die Verstorbenen in der Unterwelt. Über jene Unterwelt regierte Erlik in deren tiefstem Punkt in einem Schloss.

statement.id: Erlik dianggap penyebab penyakit dan kematian serta hakim bagi orang mati, yang memerintah dari sebuah istana di titik terdalam dunia bawah.
statement.en: Erlik is held to cause sickness and death and to judge the dead, ruling from a castle at the deepest point of the underworld.
